items.body:
## Summary

A brand-new CLI session can receive a **dead, unrelated session's** async delegation results as `[ASYNC DELEGATION BATCH COMPLETE]` turns, seconds after boot. Reproduced live (delivered_at exactly 2s after the new process started) and deterministically in isolation.

## Symptom

Start `hermes`, do nothing. If ANY previous hermes process on the machine dispatched `delegate_task` subagents and exited before their completions were injected, the new session receives those completions as if it had dispatched them — full conversation payload (goal, context, result summary) from a session the user may have long abandoned.

Observed live: old session `A` dispatched a batch at 16:44, completed 16:49, process exited. New CLI process started 16:59:52; the foreign batch was injected into it at 16:59:54.

## Root cause (3 layers)

1. **Durable completions rehydrate unconditionally.** `ProcessRegistry.__init__` (tools/process_registry.py:177) calls `restore_undelivered_completions()` (tools/async_delegation.py:266), which enqueues every `delivery_state='pending'` row regardless of `origin_session`. Since #63494 made completions durable, a fresh process inherits other (dead) sessions' events at startup.

2. **The CLI idle drain's ownership key resolves to empty.** cli.py idle drain does `_drain_sk = get_current_session_key(default="")`. In a CLI process the approval contextvar is only bound DURING a turn (set/reset around agent.run), and `HERMES_SESSION_KEY` is not in the CLI environment. So while idle `_drain_sk == ""` and `drain_notifications` takes its documented "legacy consume-everything" branch (tools/process_registry.py:1209-1213).

3. **The CLI post-turn drain passes no filter at all.** `drain_notifications()` bare — unconditional consume-everything.

The ownership filter added for #58684/#55578 is effectively dead code on the CLI: both CLI drain sites bypass it. That was SAFE before durability, because the in-memory queue could only contain events created by this very process. The durable restore silently broke that invariant.

## Why existing fixes don't cover this

- #63317 (open) enforces ownership on all drain paths — TUI only; CLI call sites untouched.
- #63856 (open) interrupts subagents on /new — different failure mode (in-flight); here the delegation completed and persisted before the old process exited.
- 75efd7396 ("never resurrect ended sessions for delegation completions") — gateway only.

## Reproduction (deterministic, no agent needed)

```python
# process 1 (old session) — persist a completed, undelivered delegation, then exit
import tools.async_delegation as ad
ad._persist_dispatch({"delegation_id": "d1", "session_key": "OLD_SESSION_A", ...})
ad._persist_completion({...,"session_key": "OLD_SESSION_A", "summary": "SECRET"}, {...})

# process 2 (new CLI session B)
from tools.process_registry import process_registry   # __init__ restores 1 event
process_registry.drain_notifications()                 # consumed by session B — LEAK
```

## Fix direction (PR follows)

Bug-class fix at the chokepoint, not the symptom:
- stamp restored events (`restored=True`, in-memory only) in `restore_undelivered_completions`
- `drain_notifications`' unfiltered legacy branch never consumes restored events (fail closed; requeue keeps them pending on disk for the owning session's `--resume`)
- both CLI drain sites pass a positive-ownership callback bound to the CLI's real `session_id` (compression-lineage aware, mirroring the TUI's `_session_owns_notification_event`)
- regression tests: fresh-process restore + unfiltered/foreign drains must not consume; owner drain must; keyless same-process events keep legacy behavior.

items.body:
## Environment
- Hermes Agent v0.18.2 (2026.7.7.2), install method: git, macOS (Darwin 25.5.0, arm64)
- One-shot mode: `hermes -p <profile> -z "run: uv run pytest ..."`

## Reproducibility
- Symptom A reproduced **2/2** (deterministic in our environment).
- Symptom B occurred **2/2** on long runs, but at different points / with different manifestations.

## Symptom A — single passing test returns exit 0 with completely empty stdout (2/2)
Asking the agent to run one pytest test (`uv run pytest path/to/test_file.py::test_name -q`) returns exit code 0 and **zero bytes of stdout/stderr** as observed by the agent. `pytest -q` always prints at least a summary line (`1 passed in ...`), so the child's output is being swallowed between the child process and the agent's tool-output view. The test's fixtures contain dummy AWS-style secret literals, so an output-redaction layer is a plausible suspect, but we have not confirmed causation.

## Symptom B — long suite (~1400 tests): output stream truncated mid-run (2/2, variable)
- Run 1: agent reported the execution was interrupted near a test handling dummy long-lived-credential fixture strings; no pytest summary was produced.
- Run 2: visible pytest progress stopped abruptly at ~20% (right after an `F` and one further `.`); no further output, no summary — while the Hermes session itself survived and completed its turn normally.

## Expected
Child output should reach the model, with secrets redacted **in place** (e.g. `[REDACTED]`) if needed, and any truncation should be explicit (a visible marker). Silent suppression causes agents to draw wrong conclusions ("the test produced no output" / "the process was killed") and makes running test suites in one-shot mode unreliable.

## Notes
- Our repo is private; reproduction pattern: a pytest suite with non-trivial output volume whose fixtures include dummy secret-shaped strings (e.g. AWS-style access key literals).
- Happy to run diagnostic builds or provide more traces.

items.title: Desktop session can hang indefinitely after native vision replay inflates Codex request

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

items.body:
## Summary

A Hermes Desktop session can remain indefinitely "active" after repeated native `vision_analyze` calls inflate the replayed request far beyond the practical provider request size. The provider may first return HTTP 507 (`exceeded request buffer limit while retrying upstream`), but a later retry can then wait indefinitely because Hermes disables its no-byte TTFB watchdog for large requests.

The Python session worker remains alive, the session row has no `ended_at` or `end_reason`, and Desktop continues to present the turn as running even though no tool or API progress occurs.

This was observed several times in one day during screenshot-heavy browser/UI work.

## Environment

- Hermes Agent: v0.18.2 (2026.7.7.2)
- Surface: Hermes Desktop
- Host: macOS
- Provider: `openai-codex`
- Model: `gpt-5.6-sol`
- Install: git checkout, one upstream commit behind at time of observation

## Observed behavior

A long-running Desktop turn repeatedly captured screenshots and passed them to native vision analysis. Representative log lines showed individual native vision tool results contributing very large persisted outputs:

```text
tools.vision_tools: vision_analyze: native fast path
agent.tool_executor: tool vision_analyze completed (0.01s, 175030 chars)
```

As more images were analyzed, the request-size estimate grew well beyond the normal model context:

```text
Disabling openai-codex no-byte TTFB watchdog for large request (context=~1,252,749 tokens >= 10000). Waiting for backend response instead.
...
Disabling openai-codex no-byte TTFB watchdog for large request (context=~1,296,546 tokens >= 10000). Waiting for backend response instead.
...
Disabling openai-codex no-byte TTFB watchdog for large request (context=~1,383,453 tokens >= 10000). Waiting for backend response instead.
```

The provider eventually reported:

```text
HTTP 507: exceeded request buffer limit while retrying upstream
```

Hermes retried. A subsequent oversized request produced no completion or error for more than 13 minutes. During that time:

- the `tui_gateway.slash_worker` process was still alive but idle;
- the session had no `ended_at` or `end_reason`;
- no new API/tool completion lines appeared;
- Desktop still showed the session as active.

The last completed action was a `vision_analyze` tool result, not a final assistant response.

## Expected behavior

1. Native vision/image data should not accumulate as giant replay payloads in active conversation history.
2. Vision tool results should obey an effective replay/context cap, even when the native fast path is used.
3. Hermes should detect that the next provider request exceeds a practical/model/provider limit and compact, strip image payloads, or fail recoverably before sending it.
4. An oversized request must retain a finite hard timeout. Disabling the no-byte watchdog should not allow an indefinite wait.
5. If the provider rejects or stalls on an oversized request, the turn should transition to a visible failed/recoverable state rather than leaving a live idle worker and an apparently active session.

## Reproduction outline

1. Start a Hermes Desktop session using OpenAI Codex.
2. Perform screenshot-heavy UI work in one turn.
3. Repeatedly call `vision_analyze` on screenshots using the native fast path.
4. Continue until many image-analysis tool results are present in active history.
5. Observe request-size estimates grow far beyond the configured model context.
6. Observe HTTP 507 or a later request that waits indefinitely with the large-request TTFB watchdog disabled.

The source screenshots and session contents are private, but the failure is visible from generic request-size, tool-output-size, provider-error, process-state, and session-state evidence.

## Root-cause hypothesis

The native vision path appears to make image content available to the model in a form that is subsequently retained/replayed with the session. Repeated screenshots therefore multiply request size. This may bypass normal text tool-output caps or count image/data payloads differently during preflight compression. Once the request is extremely large, the Codex path explicitly disables the no-byte TTFB watchdog, converting an oversized request failure into a potentially unbounded wait.

## Related issues

- #32156 tracks the broader long-session/tool-output/provider-stall problem.
- #23570 discussed native image replay bloat; its closing comment explicitly said the architectural replay-bloat fix (persist paths and rebuild image data only when needed) remained out of scope and deserved separate work.
- #54465 fixed a different compression-timeout wedge and persistent cooldown behavior. This report occurred on a version containing that fix and is not limited to preflight compression.

## Suggested acceptance criteria

- Persist lightweight image references/attachment metadata rather than replaying large inline image payloads on every later request.
- Apply replay-safe size limits to native vision results and image-bearing messages.
- Include image payload cost in preflight context/request-size decisions.
- Refuse, strip, or compact requests that exceed the provider/model request budget.
- Keep a finite configurable hard timeout for large Codex requests even when the short no-byte TTFB watchdog is disabled.
- Mark the turn failed/recoverable and clean up the worker if the provider request reaches that hard timeout.
- Add a regression test with repeated synthetic image/vision results proving request growth remains bounded and the session cannot remain indefinitely active after a provider-size rejection.

items.title: process(action='poll') hangs indefinitely on already-exited background process

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

items.body:
## Description

`process(action="poll")` hung for **30 minutes** (until gateway idle timeout at 1800s) when called on a background process that had already exited. The process was started via `terminal(background=true)` and had completed before the poll call.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Start a background process: `terminal(command="...", background=true)` → returns `session_id`
2. The process completes (exits)
3. Call `process(action="poll", session_id="<id>")` on the now-exited process
4. The poll call hangs indefinitely instead of returning `{"status": "exited", ...}`

## Expected Behavior

`poll()` should return immediately with `status: "exited"` (or `"not_found"` if the session was cleaned up) — it is a read-only status query.

## Actual Behavior

The tool call never returns. The agent loop blocks on the tool execution until the gateway idle timeout (1800s) fires.

## Environment

- Hermes Agent: commit `861d69c7b` (main)
- OS: Linux 6.8.0-134-generic
- Gateway mode (Telegram)
- Model: deepseek-v4-pro:cloud (via ollama-launch)

## Gateway Log

```
2026-07-14 17:02:03 — agent calls process(action="poll") on proc_5bd40bea5f3d
2026-07-14 17:32:23 — ERROR gateway.run: Agent idle for 1801s (timeout 1800s)
  last_activity=executing tool: process | iteration=40/60 | tool=process
```

## Analysis

The `poll()` method in `tools/process_registry.py` (line 1301) calls `self.get(session_id)` which should return `None` → `not_found` for a missing session, or return the session with `exited=True`. The hang suggests either:

1. `_reconcile_local_exit()` (line 1311) is blocking on a lock or subprocess call
2. `session._lock` (line 1313) is held by a dead reader thread
3. The session lookup itself is blocking

## Impact

Medium — blocks the agent for the full idle timeout (30 min default), but the gateway recovers correctly and preserves the conversation context on retry.

items.title: Context compression can fabricate user turns and flip session language; poisoned summary persists across compaction cycles

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

items.body:
### Summary

During a long cron session, context compression produced a summary that (a) switched the entire summary to a different language (Dutch) than the session (English), and (b) fabricated a "User asked: ..." turn that never happened (the session was a cron run with no user messages). The poisoned summary was then injected back into the session as the `[CONTEXT COMPACTION — REFERENCE ONLY]` block, survived two further compaction cycles (each one re-summarized the previous Dutch summary, so it never recovered), and the final user-facing reply followed the summary's language instead of the session's.

### Environment

- `nousresearch/hermes-agent:v2026.7.1` (stock image, digest-pinned)
- `compression.enabled: true`, `threshold: 0.47`, `target_ratio: 0.2`, `abort_on_summary_failure: false`
- `agents.compression.provider: custom`, `model: gpt-4o-mini` (OpenAI API)
- Session: a scheduled cron job using an MoA council preset; 65 aggregation rounds; compaction fired 3 times (before rounds 18, 28, 55 in the MoA trace)

### What the trace shows

- Rounds 1-17: all inputs and outputs English. No Dutch anywhere in the inputs (verified across the full 34 MB trace).
- Round 18: first `[CONTEXT COMPACTION]` block appears, fully in Dutch, beginning with an invented `## Historical Task Snapshot / User asked: 'Waar zijn de bestanden gedownload van het kennisgestuurde systeem?'` plus a Dutch `## Goal` and `## Completed Actions` list (the actions themselves corresponded to real tool calls, translated).
- Rounds 18-65: every subsequent compaction block stays Dutch; reference/aggregator outputs remain English in 63 of 65 rounds, but the final reply delivered to the messaging platform was Dutch.

### Why this matters

The compaction block's own header says "treat as background reference, NOT as active instructions", but a summary that invents user turns is a context-integrity failure: downstream turns can act on (or, as here, mirror) history that never existed. Language flip is the visible symptom; fabricated user asks are the dangerous part.

### Suggested hardening

1. Validate the summary before injecting it: reject/retry when its language differs from the dominant session language (cheap heuristic or a langid pass).
2. Never let the summarizer emit `User asked:` content in sessions that contain no user role messages (cron/agent-only sessions); template that section out.
3. When a summary fails validation, fall back to truncation rather than injecting it, or honor `abort_on_summary_failure` for validation failures too.
4. Consider re-summarizing from original turns rather than summarizing the previous summary, so one bad compaction does not poison all later ones.

Workaround on our side: moved `agents.compression.model` to a stronger model. Happy to share redacted trace excerpts.

items.title: Feature request: integrated tunnel command for remote access (Tailscale / Cloudflare) without Hermes Cloud

labels.name: duplicate
labels.description: This issue or pull request already exists

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

labels.name: comp/dashboard
labels.description: Web dashboard / control panel UI (dashboard/, landing)

labels.name: sweeper:not-planned
labels.description: Sweeper: closed per standing maintainer policy (design direction)

items.body:
## Problem

Hermes is intentionally local-first — its real value is the persistent memory, skills, and OAR vault plus the local toolchain. But the only sanctioned way to reach the **dashboard** (or the backend gateway) from another device — phone, laptop, while away from the desk — is *manual* tunnel setup:

1. keep the server bound to `127.0.0.1`,
2. stand up Cloudflare Tunnel / Tailscale `serve` / ngrok yourself,
3. point `dashboard.public_url` at it,
4. hope it survives a reboot.

This is non-obvious, scattered across source/help text, and has no reboot persistence. The `--insecure` flag is now a documented no-op (June 2026 hardening), so you *must* do the tunnel dance if you want remote access.

**Hermes Cloud** solves remote access, but: (a) it costs money, and (b) it starts from a clean slate — no local memory, no skills, no OAR vault. For users who've invested in a local-first setup, Cloud is a non-starter.

## Proposal

A first-class, integrated tunnel command that *orchestrates an existing external tunnel* and preserves the current security model:

```
hermes tunnel up --provider tailscale|cloudflare [--dashboard] [--backend]
```

Behavior:
- Keeps the target server bound to **127.0.0.1 only** — never `0.0.0.0`.
- Spawns the provider tunnel (`tailscale serve`, or `cloudflared tunnel`) against `localhost:PORT`.
- Enforces existing auth (`dashboard.basic_auth` / OAuth) — respects the June 2026 hardening; a non-loopback bind requires an auth provider.
- Prints the resulting URL (tailnet URL, or Cloudflare-assigned hostname).
- Optionally registers a startup task so it survives reboot, plus a matching `hermes tunnel down` to tear it down.

Nice-to-haves:
- `hermes dashboard --tunnel tailscale|cloudflare` convenience alias.
- Auto-populate `dashboard.public_url` once the tunnel is live.

## Why this fits Hermes design

- It's an **edge capability** (a CLI command + skill), not a new core model tool — consistent with the Footprint Ladder in AGENTS.md.
- It preserves the project's own recommended pattern: *bind loopback + tunnel to keep it local*.
- It keeps the user's local-first data sovereignty (memory, skills, OAR) intact while removing the one real downside of local hosting: being chained to the desk.

## Use case

I run Hermes on a Windows workstation at home. I want to use Hermes from my phone while away, or from a laptop, **without** paying for Cloud and **without** losing my accumulated memory/skills. Today this is achievable with `tailscale serve https://localhost:9119` + `dashboard.basic_auth`, but it took digging through source to find the right knobs (`public_url`, `basic_auth`, the `--insecure` no-op) and there is no reboot-persistence story. A single `hermes tunnel up --provider tailscale` would make the local-first workflow actually portable.

## Non-goals

- Not a request to *build* a Tunnel/Cloudflare competitor — just orchestrate the existing tools.
- Not requesting public-internet exposure by default (Funnel). Tailscale `serve` stays tailnet-private; Cloudflare would be opt-in and still auth-gated.

## Environment

- Hermes Agent (NousResearch/hermes-agent), Windows 10
- Dashboard on `127.0.0.1:9119` (returns HTTP 200)
- Tailscale 1.98.4 installed and daemon running
- `config.yaml` already exposes `dashboard.basic_auth` and `dashboard.public_url`, but no command/UI wires them to a live tunnel

items.title: [Bug]: Windows Desktop IPC bridge unavailable — built preload.cjs missing from release/win-unpacked after update

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

labels.name: sweeper:risk-platform-windows
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break or behave differently on native Windows

items.body:
## Summary

On Windows, after updating the Hermes Desktop app, the packaged build fails with **`Desktop IPC bridge is unavailable`** because the Electron preload script `preload.cjs` is **missing from the unpacked release tree**. `window.hermesDesktop` is therefore `undefined`, so every IPC call from the renderer fails.

This is a **distinct root cause** from issue #52945 (which blames `HERMES_WEB_DIST` env-var inheritance). That fix will NOT resolve this case. This report documents the missing-file mechanism, which appears to be un-filed and unfixed.

## Environment

- Windows 10/11, git-based install (`~/.hermes/hermes-agent`)
- Hermes CLI/agent version: v0.18.2 (observed)
- Hermes Desktop: packaged `release/win-unpacked` Electron app

## Root cause

The Electron renderer resolves the preload via:

```js
window.hermesDesktop = require('electron').remote ... // via
path.join(__dirname, 'preload.cjs')
```

The source preload exists and is tracked:

```
apps/desktop/electron/preload.cjs   ✅ tracked in git
```

But the **built** copy lives in a tree that is entirely **gitignored** and only populated by electron-builder during `npm run dist` / the desktop self-update:

```
apps/desktop/release/win-unpacked/resources/app.asar.unpacked/electron/preload.cjs  ❌ gitignored, sometimes absent
```

Verification on the affected machine:

```
$ git check-ignore "apps/desktop/release/win-unpacked/resources/app.asar.unpacked/electron/preload.cjs"
apps/desktop/release/win-unpacked/resources/app.asar.unpacked/electron/preload.cjs
# => IGNORED — git pull never touches it
$ git ls-files apps/desktop/release | head
# => (empty) release/ is entirely gitignored
```

Two consequences:

1. **`hermes update` (CLI)** runs `_cmd_update_impl` → `git pull --ff-only` of the Python source + pip/uv dependency sync. It does **not** invoke electron-builder, and because `release/` is gitignored, it never touches the built `preload.cjs`. So the CLI update path is safe for the desktop.
2. **The in-app / desktop self-update** rebuilds `release/win-unpacked` via electron-builder (`hermes desktop --build-only` → electron-builder `--dir`). The packaged `app.asar.unpacked/electron/` layout can be **incomplete after `npm run dist`** — i.e., electron-builder's file list does not reliably include `preload.cjs` at that unpacked path. Additionally, a running `hermes.exe` locks `release/win-unpacked` files during rebuild (see #41178), so the rebuild can silently produce a partial tree.

Because the desktop app is launched from `release/win-unpacked`, a missing `preload.cjs` there → `main.cjs` can't find it → `window.hermesDesktop` undefined → "Desktop IPC bridge is unavailable."

## Repro

1. Install / update Hermes Desktop on Windows (in-app self-update, or fresh `npm run dist`).
2. Launch the packaged `release/win-unpacked/Hermes.exe`.
3. Open DevTools in the renderer; evaluate `window.hermesDesktop`.
4. Observe `undefined` → IPC-dependent features fail with "Desktop IPC bridge is unavailable."

## Working fix (what we do manually today)

Copy the tracked source preload into the unpacked path:

```bat
copy "C:\Users\<user>\.hermes\hermes-agent\apps\desktop\electron\preload.cjs" ^
     "C:\Users\<user>\.hermes\hermes-agent\apps\desktop\release\win-unpacked\resources\app.asar.unpacked\electron\preload.cjs"
```

After this copy, `window.hermesDesktop` is defined and the IPC bridge works. This survives subsequent **CLI** `hermes update` runs (gitignored tree, not rebuilt), but is re-lost whenever the desktop self-update rebuilds `release/win-unpacked`.

## Suggested permanent fix

1. **Add `preload.cjs` to electron-builder's file list** for the Windows target so it is deterministically present in `app.asar.unpacked/electron/` after `npm run dist`.
2. **Add a packaging-verification step** (CI or post-build script) that asserts `preload.cjs` exists at the expected unpacked path before a desktop release is published.
3. **Consider bundling the preload into the main `app.asar`** (or resolving it from the tracked source path at runtime) so its presence no longer depends on an easily-missed unpacked file.
4. **Gate the desktop self-update on closing the running `hermes.exe`** (or use a side-by-side staging dir + atomic swap, like `_atomic_replace_dir` does for the Python tree) to avoid the file-lock-induced partial build from #41178.

## Related

- #52945 — same error string, but different root cause (`HERMES_WEB_DIST` env inheritance). Cross-linking to show this is a separate sub-case.
- #41178 — self-update fails because running `hermes.exe` locks `release/win-unpacked` files (partial build).
- #38407 — Windows Desktop fails after update: incomplete git checkout → missing components.
- #52764 — `hermes update` produces broken Desktop asar when git pull adds npm deps not in electron-builder file list.
- #53770 — update leaves stale `app.asar` with old config.

## Labels (suggested)

`type/bug` `comp/desktop` `platform/windows` `P2` (this breaks the desktop entirely for affected Windows users)

## Summary

After enabling GitHub Copilot MCP, Hermes conversations immediately fail with HTTP 400 schema validation errors. Providers reject the tool list because `mcp__github__search_issues` carries a corrupted `dependentRequired` field: property-name **strings** are rewritten into empty object schemas.

Confirmed on **xAI (xai-oauth)**, **OpenAI API**, and **openai-codex**. One bad tool schema aborts the entire turn (non-retryable client error).

## Environment

- Hermes: **v0.18.2 (2026.7.7.2)** · upstream `7e84d2b5`
- Install: git (`~/.hermes/hermes-agent`)
- Host: WSL2 Ubuntu on Windows
- MCP server: `https://api.githubcopilot.com/mcp/`
- Culprit tool: `mcp__github__search_issues`

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure GitHub Copilot MCP:

```yaml
mcp_servers:
  github:
    transport: http
    url: https://api.githubcopilot.com/mcp/
    headers:
      Authorization: Bearer <token>
```

2. Start Hermes TUI/CLI (any session that loads MCP tools).
3. Send any message with xAI, OpenAI, or Codex as the active provider.
4. Observe non-retryable HTTP 400; no useful model reply.

### Minimal sanitizer repro

```bash
cd ~/.hermes/hermes-agent
./venv/bin/python - <<'PY'
from tools.schema_sanitizer import _sanitize_node
import json
schema = {
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "owner": {"type": "string"},
    "repo": {"type": "string"},
  },
  "dependentRequired": {
    "owner": ["repo"],
    "repo": ["owner"],
  },
}
print(json.dumps(_sanitize_node(schema, path="test").get("dependentRequired"), indent=2))
PY
```

**Actual (broken):**

```json
{
  "owner": [{"type": "object", "properties": {}}],
  "repo": [{"type": "object", "properties": {}}]
}
```

**Expected:**

```json
{
  "owner": ["repo"],
  "repo": ["owner"]
}
```

## Expected vs Actual

| | |
|--|--|
| **Expected** | Valid JSON Schema `dependentRequired` maps (`dict[str, list[str]]`) are preserved when MCP tools are sanitized and sent to providers. |
| **Actual** | `_sanitize_node` recurses into `dependentRequired` value lists, treats property-name strings as bare schemas, and rewrites them to `{"type":"object","properties":{}}`. Providers reject the request with HTTP 400. |

## Evidence

### xAI

```text
HTTP 400: {"code":"invalid-argument","error":"Invalid request content: Schema validation failed:
[standard_violation] /dependentRequired/owner/0: {\"type\":\"object\",\"properties\":{}} is not of type \"string\";
[standard_violation] /dependentRequired/repo/0: {\"type\":\"object\",\"properties\":{}} is not of type \"string\""}
```

### OpenAI / Codex

```text
HTTP 400: Invalid schema for function 'mcp__github__search_issues':
{'type': 'object', 'properties': {}} is not of type 'string'.
param: tools[N].parameters  code: invalid_function_parameters
```

### Request dump

From `~/.hermes/sessions/request_dump_*.json`, the tool parameters for `mcp__github__search_issues` include:

```json
"dependentRequired": {
  "owner": [{"type": "object", "properties": {}}],
  "repo": [{"type": "object", "properties": {}}]
}
```

Agent log:

```text
MCP server 'github' (HTTP): registered 51 tool(s): ... mcp__github__search_issues ...
API call failed ... Non-retryable client error: Error code: 400 ...
```

## Root Cause

File: `tools/schema_sanitizer.py` → `_sanitize_node`

The pass-through set for non-schema sibling keywords includes `required`, `enum`, and `examples`, but **not** `dependentRequired`.

The same function already documents this failure mode for `required`:

> Recursing into these with `_sanitize_node()` would mis-interpret literal strings like `"path"` as bare-string schemas and replace them with `{"type": "object"}` dicts.

`sanitize_tool_schemas()` is invoked from `model_tools.py` for the full tool list (including MCP-derived tools), so any MCP tool that ships `dependentRequired` is corrupted before the API call.

Trigger observed: GitHub Copilot MCP tool `search_issues`. Any other MCP tool using `dependentRequired` would hit the same path.

## Suggested Fix

1. In `_sanitize_node`, treat `dependentRequired` like `required` (deep-copy / pass-through; do **not** recurse list items as schemas). Values must remain `dict[str, list[str]]`.
2. Add a regression test in `tests/tools/test_schema_sanitizer.py` covering a GitHub-MCP-shaped `dependentRequired` fixture.

## Workaround

```yaml
mcp_servers:
  github:
    enabled: false
```

Then start a new session / restart gateway. Chat works without GitHub MCP. Re-enabling without a sanitizer fix restores the 400.

## Impact

- **High:** With GitHub MCP enabled, every model turn can fail with a non-retryable 400 before any assistant text is produced.
- Disabling GitHub MCP restores chat but removes those tools.
- Not limited to one provider; switching models does not help while the bad tool remains registered.

items.title: [Bug]: Context-file discovery falls back to the Hermes install tree and loads its contributor AGENTS.md as project context

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

items.body:
### Bug Description

When working-directory resolution falls back to **os.getcwd(**) and the backend was launched from, or self-spawns into, the Hermes install or source tree (which is the desktop app default), context-file discovery reads that tree's own **AGENTS.md**. That file is the contributor development guide (about 73 KB). It is injected into the system prompt under "The following project context files have been loaded and should be followed", capped at 20,000 characters. An agent configured with its own **SOUL.md** then behaves like a Hermes contributor. The soul still loads; it is outweighed by the development guide.

This has a security dimension: a directory picked by a resolution fallback, not by the user, gains system-prompt authority, and nothing in the UI or logs records that it happened.

### Steps to Reproduce

Reproducible without a model, on a fresh clone of main:

```python
import os
from agent.runtime_cwd import resolve_context_cwd
from agent.prompt_builder import build_context_files_prompt

os.chdir("<hermes install or source tree>")   # the desktop backend's default cwd
os.environ.pop("TERMINAL_CWD", None)
out = build_context_files_prompt(cwd=resolve_context_cwd(), skip_soul=True)
assert "AGENTS.md" in out   # the contributor guide is now in the system prompt

```

Desktop path: set terminal.cwd to a path that does not exist, start a session on that profile, and ask the agent what it is working on. It reports the hermes-agent codebase. 

**_completion_cwd** (tui_gateway/server.py) checks **isdir**, the check fails, and it silently returns **os.getcwd()**, which on the desktop is the app install directory.

### Expected Behavior

Context-file discovery should never resolve to the Hermes install or source tree. An invalid configured t**erminal.cwd** should warn, or fail at startup, rather than silently resolve to the launch directory.

### Actual Behavior

The install tree's **AGENTS.md** is loaded and marked as project context to follow. On a fresh clone launched in-tree, about 18 KB of the development guide is injected into the system prompt. Nothing in the UI or logs indicates the working directory is wrong or which context files were loaded.

### Affected Component

Agent Core (conversation loop, context compression, memory)

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

_No response_

### Debug Report

```shell
This bug is environment-independent and reproduces on a clean clone of main with the Python snippet in Steps to Reproduce. I am omitting the full hermes debug share upload to avoid publishing local config. OS, Python, and Hermes versions are provided below, and I am happy to supply specific logs on request.
```

### Operating System

macOS 26.5.2

### Python Version

3.14.5

### Hermes Version

0.18.2 (built from main, commit 7e84d2b5a)

### Additional Logs / Traceback (optional)

```shell

```

### Root Cause Analysis (optional)

**resolve_context_cwd()** in **agent/runtime_cwd.py** returned a configured path without validating it, unlike **resolve_agent_cwd()**, so an invalid path or the install tree could steer discovery. When it returns **None**, **build_context_files_prompt()** in **agent/prompt_builder.py** falls back to **os.getcwd()**, which for a desktop-spawned backend is the install tree, and **_load_agents_md()** then reads the contributor **AGENTS.md**. Separately, **_completion_cwd()** and **_default_session_cwd()** in **tui_gateway/server.py** silently fall back to **os.getcwd()** on an invalid configured terminal.cwd, while **_set_session_cwd()** raises on the same input.

### Proposed Fix (optional)

Two changes, PR ready: 

(1) **agent/runtime_cwd.py** validates the configured cwd in **resolve_context_cwd()** and never returns the package or source root.

(2) **agent/prompt_builder.py** skips project-context discovery when the resolved cwd is the install tree, which covers the **cwd=None** to **os.getcwd()** fallback. Verified to close every trigger case while a normal workspace **AGENTS.md** still loads. I will link the PR here.

### Are you willing to submit a PR for this?

- [x] I'd like to fix this myself and submit a PR

items.title: Hosted-agent rebootstrap ignores newer session while local tokens still look healthy

labels.name: sweeper:risk-security-boundary
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may affect sandboxing, auth, credentials, or sensitive data

items.body:
## Summary

Hosted Hermes Cloud agents can enter a restart loop when NAS replaces a bootstrap session. NAS mints a replacement, revokes the old session, pushes `HERMES_AUTH_JSON_REBOOTSTRAP`, and restarts the machine. The boot helper currently applies the replacement only when the local `providers.nous` entry is already quarantined.

If the old local tokens still look healthy at boot, the helper returns `not_terminal`. The next refresh uses the now-revoked session, receives `invalid_grant`, and triggers another NAS self-heal cycle.

## Production evidence

Observed on hosted instance `cmrfv8zyr00b8jr0c8bjx14af`:

1. NAS minted a replacement bootstrap session and revoked the prior session.
2. Container boot logged `[rebootstrap] no-op (not_terminal)`.
3. The next refresh was rejected with `Refresh session has been revoked`.
4. Hermes quarantined OAuth state and NAS restarted the machine again.

The same machine recorded 74 uptime resets in the sampled four-day window.

## Expected behavior

When the orchestrator seed has an `obtained_at` later than the local session, boot should apply it even if the local entry has not yet observed the revocation. Older, equal, malformed, or incomparable seeds must remain no-ops so a retained env value cannot roll credentials backward.

items.body: # [Bug] Desktop sidebar duplicates a project on Windows — `D:\...` vs `D:/...` path normalization ## Summary On Windows, a project folder shows **twice** in the Desktop sidebar: once as the project and once as a duplicate sub-structure, each containing the same branches/sessions. This is the **Windows-specific root cause** of the symptom reported in #52811. In my environment the sidebar renders: ``` IVODIMITROV-UNIVERSE 98 ├── master 37 └── master 61 IVODIMITROV-UNIVERSE 98 ├── master 37 └── master 61 ``` `37 + 61 = 98`, and the two top-level blocks are visually identical. There is only **one** project row in the backend `projects.tree` response — but the project contains one repo rendered with **two different path spellings**: - repo node: `D:\IvoDimitrov-Universe` (backslash) - inner worktree/lane group: `D:/IvoDimitrov-Universe` (forward slash) The backend treats these as two distinct directories, and the Desktop then re-injects the real main checkout from `git worktree list`, producing the doubled tree. ## Root cause The authoritative tree builder (`tui_gateway/project_tree.py`) and the renderer (`apps/desktop/src/app/chat/sidebar/projects/workspace-groups.ts`) have explicit Windows path normalization (`_is_windows_path`, `pathKey`, `comparisonSegments`, case-insensitive comparison). **However**, the lane id / repo id is emitted using the *raw* session `cwd` spelling: - `_build_repos()` builds `lane_identity = _lane_key(placement["lane_key"])` and `repo_identity = _path_key(entry["repo_key"])`. - The session `cwd` from `state.db` is stored with backslashes (`D:\IvoDimitrov-Universe`), while the injected main-checkout lane from the live `git worktree list` probe comes back with forward slashes (`D:/IvoDimitrov-Universe`). - The comparison keys normalize, so the *membership* collapses correctly in `build_tree()`, but the **rendered group id/path** keeps the mismatched spelling, so the Desktop's `mergeRepoWorktreeGroups()` / `overlayRepoLanes()` see two lanes (`isMain` from git + a non-`isMain` duplicate from the backslash repo) and renders them both. No two project rows exist in `projects.db`; no two `cwd` values exist in `state.db`. It is purely a normalization mismatch between the stored `cwd` and the git-probed path inside the same repo node. ## Evidence `projects.tree` RPC (Hermes Desktop v0.18.2) returns one project `IvoDimitrov-Universe` (sessionCount 61), whose single repo contains a group with: ```json { "id": "D:/IvoDimitrov-Universe", "label": "IvoDimitrov-Universe", "path": "D:/IvoDimitrov-Universe", "isMain": false, "isKanban": false, "sessions": [] } ``` while the parent repo node is `D:\IvoDimitrov-Universe`. The `isMain: false` flag is wrong here — it should be the main checkout; the slash mismatch prevents the merge with the git-probed main lane. ## Environment - Hermes Agent / Desktop: **v0.18.2** (release 2026.7.7.2) - OS: **Windows 10/11** (host `IVODIMITROVPC`) - `state.db` / `projects.db` paths: `%LOCALAPPDATA%\hermes\` - Session `cwd` stored with backslashes; git worktree probe returns forward slashes. ## Suggested fix direction In `project_tree.py` (and mirrored in `workspace-groups.ts`), normalize the **emitted** lane/repo `id` and `path` through the same `pathKey`/`comparisonSegments` Windows-aware normalization used for membership, so the stored-`cwd` spelling and the git-probed spelling produce identical ids. The `isMain` decision should not depend on path spelling either. ## Related - #52811 — same duplicate-sidebar symptom (reported on macOS, no Windows path-normalization root cause identified) - #43483 / PR #43487 — earlier duplicate-row fix (compression lineage, different cause) ## Screenshot

items.title: [Bug]: TUI hides MoA reference blocks when the thinking section is hidden
items.body:
## Bug Description

Ink TUI hides Mixture-of-Agents reference-model output when `display.sections.thinking` is set to `hidden`.

MoA reference output is not the acting model's private reasoning. It is the user-facing process output introduced by #53855, whose stated contract is that references are shown regardless of `showReasoning` because they are the MoA process the user explicitly selected. However, the TUI stores each `moa.reference` event in a segment's generic `thinking` field, so the normal thinking-section visibility setting also suppresses the MoA reference block.

This makes `/moa` appear to skip its reference model entirely: the user sees the aggregator/final response but not the labelled reference output. The same run in the classic CLI displays the reference block correctly.

Related implementation: #53855

This is distinct from #59546, which requests progress counters and phase indicators while MoA is running. Here the reference output has already been produced and relayed, but the TUI visibility policy hides it.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Use current `main` / Hermes v0.18.2.
2. Configure the TUI display with:

   ```yaml
   display:
     interface: tui
     tool_progress: all
     show_reasoning: false
     sections:
       thinking: hidden
   ```

3. Configure an enabled MoA preset with at least one reachable reference model and an aggregator.
4. Launch the Ink TUI.
5. Run a short one-shot prompt, for example:

   ```text
   /moa Answer in one sentence: what is 2 plus 2?
   ```

6. Observe that no labelled `Reference 1/1 — xai-oauth:grok-4.5` block is visible before the aggregator response.
7. Run the same prompt in the classic CLI (`hermes --cli`) as a control. The CLI displays both the reference header and its text.

## Expected Behavior

MoA reference blocks should remain visible even when ordinary model reasoning is hidden.

A user who selects MoA should see output such as:

```text
◇ Reference 1/1 — xai-oauth:grok-4.5
2 plus 2 is 4.
```

`display.sections.thinking: hidden` should hide ordinary model reasoning/status content, not semantically distinct `moa.reference` events.

## Actual Behavior

The reference event is relayed and recorded, but its text is placed in the generic `thinking` field and is hidden by the thinking-section visibility policy. The user sees the aggregator/final response without the MoA reference block.

Classic CLI control on the same installation displays the expected reference block, confirming that reference generation and the shared callback path work.

## Affected Component

- TUI (Ink: `ui-tui/`)
- TUI gateway event path
- Display configuration interaction

## Environment

- OS: macOS 26.5.2 (25F84), Apple Silicon
- Hermes: v0.18.2 (2026.7.7.2)
- Source/install commit: `df5700ebe317ff9f2d9ea4677513e012eb68b6f4` (current `main` at verification time)
- Python: 3.11.15
- Interface: Ink TUI

## Debug Report

Not uploaded. This is a deterministic display-policy issue without an exception or traceback. The reference and aggregator calls complete normally, and the classic CLI control renders the reference correctly.

## Root Cause Analysis

`ui-tui/src/app/turnController.ts::recordMoaReference()` converts the MoA event into a generic trail segment:

```ts
this.pushSegment({
  kind: 'trail',
  role: 'system',
  text: '',
  thinking,
  thinkingTokens: estimateTokensRough(thinking)
})
```

The renderer then applies the normal `thinking` section mode to that field. `ui-tui/src/domain/details.ts` explicitly allows:

```yaml
display.sections.thinking: hidden
```

As a result, a semantically distinct `moa.reference` block inherits the visibility of ordinary model reasoning.

The existing test in `ui-tui/src/__tests__/createGatewayEventHandler.test.ts` verifies that `recordMoaReference` adds a segment when `showReasoning` is false, but it only inspects `streamSegments`. It does not render with `sections.thinking: hidden`, so the end-to-end visibility regression is not covered.

## Proposed Fix

Prefer representing MoA references as a dedicated message/segment kind rather than generic thinking, for example:

```ts
{
  kind: 'moa-reference',
  role: 'system',
  label,
  index,
  count,
  text
}
```

Then render that kind independently of the ordinary thinking-section visibility setting.

A smaller compatibility fix would explicitly exempt MoA reference segments from `thinking: hidden`, but a dedicated kind is safer because it preserves the semantic distinction between:

- transient `thinking.delta` status,
- actual model `reasoning.delta`, and
- `moa.reference` advisor output.

## Regression Test Suggestion

Add a renderer-level TUI test that:

1. Emits a `moa.reference` event.
2. Sets `showReasoning: false`.
3. Sets `sections.thinking: hidden`.
4. Renders the live/settled message block.
5. Verifies that the reference label and body are still painted.
6. Separately verifies that ordinary reasoning remains hidden.

This should test rendered output, not only the presence of a `thinking` field in `streamSegments`.

items.title: [Bug]: Desktop MoA reference events replace earlier advisor output instead of accumulating
items.body:
## Bug Description

Hermes Desktop handles every `moa.reference` event through the reasoning fallback replacement path. With two or more MoA reference models, each later reference removes the earlier reference reasoning part, so the reasoning disclosure can retain only the latest advisor output instead of one labelled block per reference.

This conflicts with the behavior introduced by #53855, which states that Desktop should append each reference as a labelled reasoning chunk and make the multi-reference MoA process visible.

Related implementation: #53855

This is distinct from #59546, which requests a progress counter and phase status. The issue here is loss of already-completed reference output in the Desktop message state.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Use current `main` / Hermes Desktop v0.18.2.
2. Configure an enabled MoA preset with at least two reachable reference models and one aggregator.
3. Select the MoA preset in Desktop or run `/moa Answer in one sentence: what is 2 plus 2?`.
4. Let the gateway emit two sequential events:

   ```text
   moa.reference(index=1, count=2, label=model-a, text=advice-a)
   moa.reference(index=2, count=2, label=model-b, text=advice-b)
   ```

5. Inspect the live assistant message's reasoning parts / Thinking disclosure after the second event.

The behavior is also deterministic from the current event-handling code: both events call `appendReasoningDelta(..., true)`, and the `replace=true` path removes all existing reasoning parts before adding the new one.

## Expected Behavior

Desktop should preserve and display one labelled block per reference model, in order:

```text
◇ Reference 1/2 — model-a
advice-a

◇ Reference 2/2 — model-b
advice-b
```

No advisor output should be discarded merely because another reference finishes later.

## Actual Behavior

`apps/desktop/src/app/session/hooks/use-message-stream/gateway-event.ts` handles `moa.reference` with:

```ts
appendReasoningDelta(sessionId, `${header}\n${body}\n\n`, true)
```

The third argument selects replacement semantics. In `apps/desktop/src/app/session/hooks/use-message-stream/index.ts`, the replacement path does:

```ts
return [...parts.filter(part => part.type !== 'reasoning'), reasoningPart(delta)]
```

Therefore the second reference removes the first reference's reasoning part and inserts only the second one. If assistant text has already appeared, the same replacement branch can instead return the existing parts unchanged, which can also prevent a late reference from being recorded.

## Affected Component

- Hermes Desktop (`apps/desktop/`)
- Gateway message-stream handling for `moa.reference`

## Environment

- Hermes: v0.18.2 (2026.7.7.2)
- Source/install commit inspected: `df5700ebe317ff9f2d9ea4677513e012eb68b6f4` (current `main` at verification time)
- Desktop event and message-state code path

## Debug Report

Not uploaded. This report is based on a deterministic source-level state transition in the current Desktop handler. No provider error or backend exception is required: two valid sequential `moa.reference` events are sufficient.

## Root Cause Analysis

`replace=true` is appropriate for `reasoning.available`, where a final non-streamed reasoning payload may replace an incomplete fallback. It is not appropriate for `moa.reference`, where each event represents a different advisor and must accumulate.

The Desktop event handler currently reuses the same replacement API for both concepts:

- `reasoning.available`: replacement/fallback semantics
- `moa.reference`: independent multi-item append semantics

The existing Desktop test suite covers reasoning rendering and preservation, but no test was found that emits two `moa.reference` events and verifies that both labelled advisors remain present.

## Proposed Fix

At minimum, do not send MoA references through the replacement path. Append them instead of calling:

```ts
appendReasoningDelta(sessionId, text, true)
```

However, a dedicated message part is safer and clearer:

```ts
{
  type: 'moa-reference',
  label,
  index,
  count,
  text
}
```

This avoids conflating:

- provider reasoning,
- fallback reasoning replacement,
- and independent MoA advisor output.

It would also allow the UI to render each reference as a separate accessible disclosure with a stable label.

## Regression Test Suggestion

Add a Desktop message-stream test that:

1. Starts a new assistant message.
2. Emits `moa.reference` for reference 1 of 2.
3. Emits `moa.reference` for reference 2 of 2.
4. Verifies that both labels and both bodies remain in message parts.
5. Completes the assistant message and verifies that both reference blocks survive reconciliation/hydration.
6. Verifies that ordinary `reasoning.available` still retains its replacement behavior.

items.title: [Bug]: Telegram adapter fails to start on default-profile gateway when multiplex_profiles: true and bot token lives in a secondary profile .env

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

labels.name: sweeper:risk-message-delivery
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may drop, duplicate, misroute, or suppress messages

items.body:
[Bug]: Telegram adapter fails to start on default-profile gateway when multiplex_profiles: true and bot token lives in a secondary profile .env

## Summary

After `hermes update` (which restarts the default-profile gateway via `launch_detached_profile_gateway_restart`), Telegram stops connecting. The gateway log shows `No bot token configured` at startup and every 60-300s reconnect attempt thereafter.

## Root cause

When `gateway.multiplex_profiles: true` and the bot token lives in `profiles/<secondary>/.env` (only there, not in `~/AppData/Local/hermes/.env`), the **default-profile gateway's** startup token resolution still fails.

- `gateway/config.py:174` (`_getenv`) reads from the active profile secret scope when one is installed; otherwise falls back to `os.environ.get(name)`.
- `gateway/run.py:2834` calls `load_gateway_config()` for the default gateway **without** an installed secret scope, so `_getenv("TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN")` falls through to `os.environ`, which is empty.
- The token lives in `profiles/therapy/.env`. The scope is only installed later, inside `_profile_runtime_scope` (`gateway/run.py:8657` -> `load_gateway_config()` for the secondary profile).
- `_apply_env_overrides` in `gateway/config.py:1471` then stores an empty token on `PlatformConfig` for the default gateway's view of Telegram.
- The Telegram adapter's `connect()` (`plugins/platforms/telegram/adapter.py:3252`) checks `self.config.token` and returns False. The reconnect watcher loops forever on the same empty config.

## Why this update triggered it (timing)

This is downstream of PR #59315 / commit `0f154e780e71c74f8a1cdccb25c97a6abd8e5a57` (issue #49415) which fixed the **secondary-profile** `load_gateway_config` path. That fix correctly scopes per-profile loads via `_profile_runtime_scope` at `gateway/run.py:8657`.

But the **default-profile gateway startup** at `gateway/run.py:2834` is still unscoped -- `load_gateway_config()` is called before any secret scope is installed, so `_getenv("TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN")` falls through to `os.environ` and returns empty.

Pre-update, the user's bot token was apparently still in `~/AppData/Local/hermes/.env` (the default profile's env), so the unscoped `os.environ.get("TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN")` worked. The token was migrated to `profiles/therapy/.env` sometime around June 19 (per `profiles/therapy/.env` mtime = `2026-06-19 19:45`). After that, every gateway restart has been a coin-flip on whether `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN` is in the default `.env` or only in the profile one -- the recent `hermes update` apparently triggered a restart that surfaced it.

## Reproduction

1. Default profile is `~/AppData/Local/hermes/`. `~/.hermes/.env` exists but contains no `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN`.
2. Create a secondary profile `therapy` with `hermes profile create therapy`.
3. Put a valid bot token only in `profiles/therapy/.env`:
   ```
   TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN=<bot-token>
   ```
4. Set `gateway.multiplex_profiles: true` in `~/.hermes/config.yaml`.
5. Restart the gateway: `hermes update` (or any flow that ends up calling `hermes gateway restart`).
6. Watch `~/.hermes/logs/gateway.log`:
   ```
   gateway.run: Connecting to telegram...
   hermes_plugins.telegram_platform.adapter: [Telegram] No bot token configured
   gateway.run: x telegram failed to connect
   gateway.run: Starting reconnection watcher for 1 failed platform(s): telegram
   ```
7. Reconnect attempts every 60s, all failing with the same error.

## Expected

Either:
- (a) `_apply_env_overrides` at default-gateway startup also reads through the active profile's secret scope when `multiplex_profiles: true` is set, OR
- (b) `load_gateway_config` for the **default** gateway, when multiplex is active, walks the profile directories (default first, then secondaries in order) to find any profile that enables + supplies the platform's token -- picking the same profile that will actually serve that platform's chats (matched via the existing channel-directory mapping).

(b) is more correct because the gateway only ever constructs one Telegram adapter regardless of how many profiles claim a Telegram channel; the token must come from whichever profile owns the chat that maps to that adapter.

## Actual

The default gateway starts with `PlatformConfig.token = ""` for Telegram. The adapter fails to connect. The reconnect watcher loops forever. Manual workaround is to put `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN=...` in `~/AppData/Local/hermes/.env` (the default profile's env), which the user has now done as an emergency workaround.

## Workaround (applied locally)

Appended the Telegram token from `profiles/therapy/.env` into `~/AppData/Local/hermes/.env` and restarted. Telegram reconnected immediately:

```
2026-07-14 17:42:52,557 INFO hermes_plugins.telegram_platform.adapter: [Telegram] Connected to Telegram (polling mode)
2026-07-14 17:42:52,657 INFO gateway.run: ✓ telegram connected (profile: therapy)
```

This is a stopgap -- it leaks the token into the default profile's env, which is the exact thing `multiplex_profiles: true` is supposed to prevent. The proper fix is upstream.

## Environment

- Hermes `0.18.2` (`bb5fc723b feat(relay): consume channel context from the connector (#64649)`)
- Python 3.11.14
- Windows 10 (LocalAppData-based HERMES_HOME)
- Fix from PR #59315 / commit `0f154e780` IS in HEAD per `git merge-base --is-ancestor 0f154e780e71c74f8a1cdccb25c97a6abd8e5a57 HEAD`

## Related

- #49415 (closed, sweeper:implemented-on-main) -- fixed the secondary-profile load path, but not the default-gateway startup path this issue describes
- #52446 (open) -- security concern in the opposite direction: secondary profile connecting with default profile's token
- #51447 (open) -- Bitwarden profile-suffixed secrets never reach platform plugins that read a fixed env var
- #51029 (closed) -- same root cause family, secondary profile's token leaks from default
- #64210 (open) -- `_apply_env_overrides` auto-activates SMS/Twilio from inherited env vars

## Proposed fix

In `gateway/run.py`, when constructing the default gateway runner with `multiplex_profiles: true`, wrap `self.config = config or load_gateway_config()` in a synthetic profile scope that includes both the default `.env` AND all `profiles/*/.env` files (in stable order -- default first, then alphabetical). This mirrors how per-profile loads already work at line 8657, but for the default gateway's startup.

Alternative (simpler, less correct): in `gateway/config.py:_apply_env_overrides`, when `multiplex_profiles: true`, also probe `profiles/*/.env` for any platform token missing in the unscoped `os.environ`. Less correct because it doesn't preserve the "this token belongs to profile X" attribution, but it would unblock the immediate symptom without redesigning the multiplexer startup.

Happy to submit a PR for either if maintainers want -- leaving the choice to the architecture owners.

items.body:
## Summary

On current `main`, the Telegram platform fails to start with:

```
ERROR hermes_plugins.telegram_platform.adapter: [Telegram] Failed to connect to Telegram: 'HTTPXRequest' object attribute 'do_request' is read-only
WARNING gateway.run: ✗ telegram failed to connect
WARNING gateway.run: No adapter could be created for any of the 1 configured platform(s).
```

Telegram never connects (the gateway continues for cron only).

## Root cause

`_instrument_polling_request()` in `plugins/platforms/telegram/adapter.py` wraps the getUpdates request by assigning an **instance** attribute:

```python
# plugins/platforms/telegram/adapter.py (~line 1999)
request.do_request = _do_request
return request
```

But `python-telegram-bot==22.6` (pinned in `pyproject.toml`) seals `HTTPXRequest` via `__slots__`:

```python
# telegram/request/_httpxrequest.py
__slots__ = ("_client", "_client_kwargs", "_http_version", "_media_write_timeout")
async def do_request(self, ...): ...
```

`do_request` is a class method and not in `__slots__`, and there is no `__dict__`, so assigning it on an instance raises `AttributeError: 'HTTPXRequest' object attribute 'do_request' is read-only`. `_instrument_polling_request` is called at ~line 3407 in all transport branches (direct / proxy / fallback), so it breaks polling startup unconditionally.

Introduced in `202be02ac` ("test(telegram): define polling progress contract", 2026-07-14). Not present in any tagged release (latest: `v2026.7.7.2`).

## Reproduce

```python
from telegram.request import HTTPXRequest        # python-telegram-bot 22.6
r = HTTPXRequest()
r.do_request = lambda *a, **k: None
# AttributeError: 'HTTPXRequest' object attribute 'do_request' is read-only
```

## Environment

- python-telegram-bot 22.6, httpx 0.28.1 (both as pinned in `pyproject.toml`)
- Hermes `main` (VERSION reports v0.18.2 / 2026.7.7.2, but built from post-tag `main`)
- Python 3.13

## Suggested fix

Attach the observational wrapper in a `__slots__`-safe way — reassign `request.__class__` to a trivial subclass that overrides `do_request` (identical slots layout, so the swap is legal), instead of setting an instance attribute:

```python
def _instrument_polling_request(self, request):
    adapter = self
    base = type(request)

    class _InstrumentedPollingRequest(base):
        __slots__ = ()
        async def do_request(self, *args, **kwargs):
            generation = _POLLING_GENERATION_CONTEXT.get()
            result = await base.do_request(self, *args, **kwargs)
            status_code, payload = result
            if generation is not None and 200 <= status_code < 300:
                try:
                    envelope = self.parse_json_payload(payload)
                except Exception:
                    pass
                else:
                    if isinstance(envelope, dict) and envelope.get("ok") is True and "result" in envelope:
                        adapter._record_polling_progress(generation)
            return result

    try:
        request.__class__ = _InstrumentedPollingRequest
    except TypeError:
        logger.debug("[%s] Could not instrument polling request", self.name)
    return request
```

Verified working against python-telegram-bot 22.6: `request.__class__ = subclass` succeeds where instance assignment fails, and polling progress (the health verifier that otherwise tears the connection down as "no progress before verifier deadline") is preserved.

items.title: bug(state): compression-split child sessions lose cwd/git_repo_root, causing project sidebar entry to disappear every compression

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

items.body:
## Summary

When a long conversation is auto-compressed, a new child session row (`end_reason='compression'` chain, `parent_session_id` set) is created to continue the lineage. This child row is inserted **without** copying `cwd` and `git_repo_root` from the parent. Because the desktop project sidebar groups sessions into a Project by longest-prefix match of `sessions.cwd` against `project_folders.path`, and because `sessions list` only shows the **tip** of the lineage, the effect is that after each compression cycle **the project appears to lose its entry from the sidebar**.

The user perceives it as "the project disappears from the sidebar every few hours" — actually the Project row in `projects.db` is fine; it just has no session claiming it anymore, because the tip session's `cwd`/`git_repo_root` are `NULL`.

## Version

- Hermes desktop `0.18.2` (release_date `2026.7.7.2`)
- Backend at `~/AppData/Local/hermes/hermes-agent`
- Host: Windows 10
- Profile: `default`

## Reproduction

1. Create a Project via `hermes project create` bound to a folder that is also a git repo.
2. Start a long TUI or desktop session inside that folder — enough that context compression will trigger. Verify:
   ```sql
   SELECT id, cwd, git_repo_root FROM sessions WHERE id = '<session>';
   ```
   Both fields are populated for the original session.
3. Let compression fire. A new session row is created with `parent_session_id = <old>` and `end_reason='compression'` on the parent.
4. Query the child:
   ```sql
   SELECT id, parent_session_id, cwd, git_repo_root FROM sessions
    WHERE parent_session_id = '<old>';
   ```
   - **Observed:** `cwd` and `git_repo_root` are both `NULL` on the child.
   - **Expected:** child inherits `cwd`/`git_repo_root` from parent (same conversation, same working directory).
5. Open the desktop UI. The project sidebar entry for that Project is gone:
   - Older ancestors are hidden (they carry `end_reason='compression'` — treated as non-tip),
   - The new tip session has `cwd = NULL`, so `workspace_key(row)` (`hermes_state.py:35`) returns `None` and it doesn't group under any Project folder.

## Real-world evidence (from my machine)

Over one week, a single conversation ("CPU扣板PCB电源树设计与功耗分析") accumulated **9 generations** from repeated compression. Every child was born with `cwd = NULL` and `git_repo_root = NULL`:

| gen | id | cwd on birth | git_repo_root on birth | end_reason |
|---:|---|---|---|---|
| #1 | `20260707_180415_e4cd9c` | `F:\...\TW公版项目-AESWITCHFE-CTC006-0001` (from initial `create_session`) | (same) | `compression` |
| #2 | `20260707_202301_72b776` | (inherited, also fine) | (same) | `compression` |
| #3 | `20260711_164025_ef3502` | **NULL** | **NULL** | `compression` |
| #4 | `20260713_180456_d996d8` | **NULL** | **NULL** | `compression` |
| #5 | `20260714_135758_887f4e` | **NULL** | **NULL** | `compression` |
| #6 | `20260714_151625_7624d2` | **NULL** | **NULL** | `compression` |
| #7 | `20260714_170605_fbed40` | **NULL** | **NULL** | `compression` |
| #8 | `20260714_170903_f619d1` | **NULL** | **NULL** | `compression` |
| #9 | `20260714_175734_035874` | **NULL** ← current tip | **NULL** | — |

Note the rate: **5 compressions within 24 hours** (2026-07-14). Every one produced a new NULL-cwd tip. Each event silently ejected the conversation from the project sidebar until I manually re-filled the fields with SQL.

Because parents #3-#8 are themselves NULL (inheriting from their own NULL parents), a single UPDATE joining on `parent_session_id` doesn't fix mid-lineage — a **recursive** backfill (repeated iterations until fixpoint, or a `WITH RECURSIVE` CTE) is needed. My workaround loop took 5 iterations to fill #5 through #9 from #4's populated cwd.

## Root cause analysis

`hermes_state.py` — `_insert_session_row` (around lines 1717-1749) has this column list on INSERT:

```
id, source, user_id, session_key, chat_id, chat_type, thread_id,
model, model_config, system_prompt, parent_session_id, cwd, started_at
```

Two problems:

1. **`git_repo_root` is not in the insert list at all.** It can only be filled later by a separate `update_session_cwd()` call (line 2126-2162). The compression path never invokes that when it forks the child.
2. **`cwd` is passed in but the compression caller doesn't propagate the parent's `cwd`.** The child inherits `parent_session_id` and `system_prompt`, but the caller supplies `cwd=None` (or omits it), so `cwd` becomes `NULL` on the child row.

Compared to gateway session upserts, which already `COALESCE(sessions.cwd, excluded.cwd)` to backfill `cwd` on conflict (line 1733), the compression-fork path has no equivalent inheritance from parent.

## Suggested fix (minimal footprint)

At the site that creates the compression-child session, resolve `cwd` and `git_repo_root` from the parent row and pass them into `create_session` / `_insert_session_row`.

Alternatively, add a defense-in-depth guarantee inside `_insert_session_row`: when `parent_session_id` is set and `cwd`/`git_repo_root` are NULL on the incoming row, `COALESCE` them from the parent. Something like a post-insert UPDATE in the same `_do`:

```sql
UPDATE sessions
   SET cwd = COALESCE(sessions.cwd,
             (SELECT p.cwd FROM sessions p WHERE p.id = sessions.parent_session_id)),
       git_repo_root = COALESCE(sessions.git_repo_root,
                       (SELECT p.git_repo_root FROM sessions p WHERE p.id = sessions.parent_session_id))
 WHERE id = ? AND parent_session_id IS NOT NULL;
```

This preserves the "don't clobber a value an earlier writer already set" invariant the existing `_insert_session_row` doc-comment guarantees (line 1706-1709).

A one-time migration to backfill existing tips would also unstick users who've already accumulated NULL-cwd tips from prior compressions — same query, but scoped to all rows where `cwd IS NULL AND parent_session_id IS NOT NULL AND EXISTS(parent with non-null cwd)`, iterated to fixpoint (or expressed as a recursive CTE) to cover multi-generation lineages like the 9-gen chain above.

## Workaround I'm using locally

Against `~/AppData/Local/hermes/state.db`, in a loop until 0 rows updated:

```sql
UPDATE sessions
   SET cwd = (SELECT p.cwd FROM sessions p WHERE p.id = sessions.parent_session_id),
       git_repo_root = (SELECT p.git_repo_root FROM sessions p WHERE p.id = sessions.parent_session_id)
 WHERE (cwd IS NULL OR cwd = '')
   AND parent_session_id IS NOT NULL
   AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM sessions p
                WHERE p.id = sessions.parent_session_id
                  AND p.cwd IS NOT NULL AND p.cwd != '');
```

Restores the project sidebar entry, but has to be re-run after every compression — which is the ongoing pain.

## Related surface

- `hermes_state.py:35 workspace_key()` — returns `None` when both fields are NULL, causing the tip row to be non-groupable.
- `projects_db.py` module docstring line 8: *"a session belongs to a project when its `cwd` lives under one of the project's folders (longest-prefix match)"* — the intended contract; the compression path violates it.
- `hermes_cli/main.py:13531` (`sessions list --workspace NEEDLE`) — same symptom via CLI: `No sessions found` for the project's own folder because the tip's `cwd` is NULL.

Happy to open a PR if the maintainers agree the fix belongs in `_insert_session_row` (adding the `COALESCE`-from-parent) rather than at the compression call site.

items.title: [Bug]: Regression — pyproject license="MIT" + setuptools>=77 build requirement breaks editable install (Windows update fails)

labels.name: sweeper:risk-compatibility
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break existing users, config, migrations, defaults, or upgrades

items.body:
## Summary

On Windows, `hermes update` fails its Python dependency step because the repo's `pyproject.toml` declares `license = "MIT"` (PEP 639 SPDX string form) while pinning `setuptools>=77.0,<83` as the build backend — but **every setuptools version in that range rejects the bare-string `license = "MIT"` form** under strict PEP 639 validation. The editable build (`uv pip install -e .` / `pip install -e .`) dies with:

```
configuration error: `project.license` must be valid exactly by one definition (2 matches found):
    - keys: 'file': {type: string}   required: ['file']
    - keys: 'text': {type: string}   required: ['text']
GIVEN VALUE: "MIT"
```

This is a **regression**: two prior issues addressed the same area and the combined result is broken.

## Regression context (please read before closing as duplicate)

- **#38353** (closed 2026-06-03) switched `license = { text = "MIT" }` → `license = "MIT"` and raised the build-backend floor to `setuptools>=77`, on the belief that `>=77` accepts the SPDX string form. **It does not.** setuptools 77–82 require either `{text: "MIT"}` or a PEP 639 SPDX *expression* config (plus `license-files`); the bare string `"MIT"` is rejected.
- **#36661** (closed 2026-06-04) upper-bounded the build requirement to `<83`, "aligning with the dev dependency pin of `setuptools==82.0.1`." But **82.0.1 is itself in the rejecting range.** So both fixes together land in a state where the declared license form is incompatible with the pinned backend.

Net effect: a clean venv (or the isolated build env uv creates during `hermes update`) cannot build `hermes-agent` at all. The build only succeeds when the venv happens to contain an *older* setuptools (<77) or a specifically-pinned 77.0.x, neither of which the current `pyproject.toml` guarantees.

## Environment

- Windows 10/11, git-based install at `~/.hermes/hermes-agent`
- Observed at commit `6997dc81` (0 commits behind `origin/main`, pulled 2026-07-14)
- Venv Python 3.11.9; `setuptools` present at 65.5.0, but the isolated build env fetches setuptools 77–82 per `build-system.requires`
- `pyproject.toml` relevant lines:
  ```toml
  [build-system]
  requires = ["setuptools>=77.0,<83"]
  build-backend = "setuptools.build_meta"

  [project]
  license = "MIT"
  license-files = ["LICENSE"]
  ```

## Repro

1. Fresh or updated git install on Windows.
2. Run `hermes update` (or `uv pip install -e .` / `pip install -e .` in the repo root).
3. The dependency step fails with the `project.license` validation error above; `hermes update` then falls back to the ZIP path, which fails with `WinError 5 Access denied` because the running Desktop app / gateway workers hold `.pyd` files locked. The install is left half-updated.

## Workaround (what we did to recover)

Pin setuptools to the one version in the range that still accepts the bare string, then build with `--no-build-isolation`:

```bat
venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pip install "setuptools==77.0.3"
venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pip install -e . --no-build-isolation
```

This works because 77.0.3 accepts `license = "MIT"` as a (deprecated-but-valid) string, whereas 77.1+ rejects it. But it is fragile: the next `hermes update` re-fetches a fresh setuptools into an isolated build env and breaks again.

## Suggested permanent fixes (any one resolves it)

1. **Make the license form and the backend version consistent.** Either:
   - Keep `license = "MIT"` **and** pin the build backend to `setuptools==77.0.3` exactly (the last version accepting the bare string), or
   - Switch to the PEP 639 dict form `license = { text = "MIT" }` (which #38353 deliberately moved *away* from) and keep `setuptools>=77`, or
   - Use the SPDX-expression form with proper `license-files` and a setuptools that supports it (>=77, but the string form specifically needs care).
2. **Add a CI job that actually runs the editable build** (`pip install -e .`) on a clean venv with the pinned `build-system.requires`, so this regression is caught before release. The previous fixes (#38353, #36661) evidently were not validated against a real isolated build.
3. **Make `hermes update`'s dependency step robust to this**: when the editable build fails on `project.license`, fall back to a known-good setuptools pin rather than the ZIP path (which then hits the unrelated `WinError 5` file-lock on Windows).

## Related

- #38353 (closed) — switched to `license = "MIT"` + `setuptools>=77`; **introduced** the incompatibility.
- #36661 (closed) — upper-bounded to `<83` aligning with `setuptools==82.0.1`; **82.x also rejects** the string form, so this cemented the break.
- #59850 (open) — *related but distinct*: Windows `hermes update` fails `uv pip install -e .` with exit 2 at `PROJECT_ROOT`. That is a cwd/layout issue; this report is the setuptools/license *validation* issue. They may surface through the same update path but have different roots.

## Labels (suggested)

`type/bug` `comp/build` `platform/windows` `regression` `P2`

## Bug Description

The Feishu adapter's `send_image_file` always fails with `[99992402] field validation failed`. Affects ALL image types: browser screenshots, rendered table PNGs, JPGs.

## Root Cause

`_build_image_upload_body` in `plugins/platforms/feishu/adapter.py` builds `CreateImageRequestBody` via lark SDK builder. The multipart form encoding is incorrect — likely wrong field names or encoding format.

```python
requests.post(
    "https://open.feishu.cn/open-apis/im/v1/images",
    headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {token}"},
    files={"image": (name, file_bytes, mime_type)},
    data={"image_type": "message"}
)
# → code=0, image_key=img_v3_xxx
```

## Reproduction

Always. Any `MEDIA:/path/to/image.png` → `send_image_file` → `[99992402]`.

## Environment

- Hermes Agent: main (latest)
- lark-oapi: 1.7.1 (latest)  
- macOS 15.5, feishu.cn

## Workaround

Bypass lark SDK for image upload. Use `requests` directly for upload + message send.
