items.title: [Bug]: vision_analyze can't read desktop/TUI uploads under a non-local terminal backend (HERMES_HOME/images not in the media-cache allowlist)

labels.name: sweeper:risk-security-boundary
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may affect sandboxing, auth, credentials, or sensitive data

items.body:
### What happened

Under a non-local terminal backend (`TERMINAL_ENV=ssh`), `vision_analyze` cannot read images that the **desktop/TUI gateway itself just saved**, because the upload directory is not in the vision resolver's media-cache allowlist.

This puts the code in direct conflict with the docs: [user-guide/features/vision](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/features/vision) states *"Images are saved to `~/.hermes/images/`"* — which is exactly the directory `tools/image_source.py` refuses to host-read.

### Repro

1. Run the agent in Docker with the terminal backend set to `ssh` (`TERMINAL_ENV=ssh`, the workaround from #54449/#63141, since the dashboard doesn't bridge `terminal.backend`).
2. Attach an image in the desktop/TUI chat. The gateway saves it to `$HERMES_HOME/images/upload_<ts>_1.png` (`tui_gateway/server.py`, clipboard-paste and byte-upload paths both use `_hermes_home / "images"`).
3. The gateway's own ingest hint tells the model to use that path:
   ```
   [The user attached an image but analysis failed.]
   [You can examine it with vision_analyze using image_url: /opt/data/images/upload_20260715_103741_1.png]
   ```
4. `vision_analyze(image_url="/opt/data/images/upload_20260715_103741_1.png")` fails:
   ```json
   {"success": false,
    "error": "sandbox returned non-image data for '/opt/data/images/upload_20260715_103741_1.png': Only base64 data is allowed"}
   ```
   or, when no terminal session exists yet in that process:
   ```json
   {"error": "'/opt/data/images/...' is not reachable inside the sandbox and no active sandbox session is available to read it"}
   ```

Telegram is unaffected — `gateway/platforms/base.py` saves photos to `$HERMES_HOME/cache/images/`, which **is** allowlisted. So vision looks healthy on one surface while being broken on another.

### Cause

`tools/image_source.py`:

- `_media_cache_roots()` returns `HERMES_HOME / "cache"`, `image_cache`, `audio_cache`, `video_cache`, `temp_vision_images`, `temp_video_files`. The flat `images/` directory is **not** included.
- `_permitted_host_read_target()` therefore returns `None` for `$HERMES_HOME/images/...` under a non-local backend, and the read is routed to `_resolve_container_fallback()`.
- In a Docker deployment with `TERMINAL_ENV=ssh`, the "sandbox" is the **remote SSH host**, while the file physically lives **inside the container**. The exec-read runs `head -c N < path | base64 | tr -d '\n'` on the wrong machine.
- That pipeline's exit status is `tr`'s, so it is `0` even when `head` fails; stdout is the `head: cannot open ...` message, which then fails `base64.b64decode(..., validate=True)` → `NotAnImage`. Hence the confusing "non-image data / Only base64 data is allowed" wording rather than "file not found".

The threat model in the module docstring assumes *agent on host, sandbox in container*. In a containerized deployment with an SSH terminal backend the relationship is inverted — the confinement sends vision **away** from the container's own data.

There is no configuration escape: `_media_cache_roots()` is hardcoded, the only `getenv` in `image_source.py` is `TERMINAL_ENV`, and the upload path in `tui_gateway/server.py` is hardcoded too.

### Expected

Images written by the gateway itself should be readable by `vision_analyze` on every surface, under any terminal backend — either by adding `HERMES_HOME/images` to `_media_cache_roots()`, or by having the desktop/TUI gateway save uploads under `HERMES_HOME/cache/images/` like the platform adapters do.

Both keep the GHSA confinement intact: the point of the allowlist is "agent-managed media caches are host-readable", and gateway uploads are exactly that.

### Version

v0.18.2 (`v2026.7.7.2`). `tools/image_source.py` on `main` is unchanged as of 2026-07-16.

### Workaround (for anyone hitting this)

Make the upload dir resolve into the cache, since `_permitted_host_read_target()` calls `.resolve()` before the allowlist check:

```bash
# inside HERMES_HOME
rm -rf images && ln -s cache/images images
```

`img_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)` in the gateway is a no-op on a symlink to an existing directory, so this survives. (This is the inverse of the case the tests cover — `test_symlink_in_cache_pointing_outside_is_not_host_read` blocks a symlink *inside* the cache pointing *out*; this one points *in*, so the bytes genuinely live in the media cache.)

### Related

- #62825 — same second error string, different cause (lazy SSH session activation). Both stack on this surface: the path isn't allowlisted → exec-read → and exec-read needs a session that doesn't exist on the first call.
- #54449 / #63141 — the `TERMINAL_ENV=ssh` workaround that makes this reachable at all.

items.title: [Bug]: Desktop App creates new session on every message when using non-default profile via remote hermes serve backend

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

items.body:
## Bug Description

When using the Hermes Desktop App connected to a remote `hermes serve` backend, every message sent under a **non-default profile** (e.g., "coder") creates a **new session** with `history=0`, instead of continuing the existing conversation.

The **default profile** works correctly — sessions persist and history is loaded. Only non-default profiles are affected.

## Environment

- **Hermes version**: 0.18.2 (release 2026.7.7.2)
- **Setup**: Desktop App (macOS) → Remote `hermes serve` backend on Linux VM (port 9120)
- **Profiles**: default, coder, coach, clawa (all visible in desktop profile switcher)
- **Model**: `glm-5.2` via `ollama-cloud` provider
- **Backend**: `hermes serve --host 0.0.0.0 --port 9120` (machine-level server, all profiles)
- **Auth**: Basic auth (username/password)

## Reproduction Steps

1. Start `hermes serve` on a remote machine (not the desktop machine)
2. Connect Desktop App to the remote backend URL
3. Select a **non-default profile** (e.g., "coder") in the desktop profile switcher
4. Send a message — agent responds correctly
5. Send a **second** message in the same chat
6. Observe: a **new session** is created with `history=0` instead of continuing the conversation

## Expected Behavior

Follow-up messages should resume the existing session with full conversation history (`history > 0`), just like the default profile does.

## Actual Behavior

Every message creates a new session. Agent logs show:

```
session=20260716_044322_3e43cc model=glm-5.2:cloud platform=desktop history=0 msg='hallo'
session=20260716_044335_579664 model=glm-5.2:cloud platform=desktop history=0 msg='wie geht es dir'
session=20260716_044752_801f94 model=glm-5.2:cloud platform=desktop history=0 msg='guten morgen'
session=20260716_044824_de53d4 model=glm-5.2:cloud platform=desktop history=0 msg='wie geht es dir'
```

Compare with default profile (works correctly):
```
session=20260713_165519_e751b0 model=glm-5.2 platform=desktop history=93 msg='Test'
session=20260713_165519_e751b0 model=glm-5.2 platform=desktop history=95 msg='wie geht es dir'
```

## Key Observations

1. **Model string difference**: Default profile sessions show `model=glm-5.2`, while coder profile sessions show `model=glm-5.2:cloud`. The `:cloud` suffix appears to come from the desktop app's model picker for ollama-cloud models.

2. **Sessions not persisted to coder's state.db**: The coder profile's `state.db` at `~/.hermes/profiles/coder/state.db` has **no new desktop sessions** since the last time it was used locally (July 13). All the new sessions created by the remote `hermes serve` process are only in memory — they never get written to the coder profile's database.

3. **Default profile works**: The same `hermes serve` process correctly persists sessions for the default profile (which uses the same `state.db` that the serve process was launched with).

4. **WebSocket disconnects**: The gui.log shows frequent WebSocket disconnects with `detached_sessions` counts, suggesting the desktop app reconnects between messages and the session routing doesn't survive reconnection for non-default profiles.

## Related PR

PR #65283 appears to address this exact issue: *"preserve routed session on profile rebind"*. The PR description states:

> Reproduced from live Desktop logs showing follow-up turns reaching new sessions with `history=0` after profile switching/reconnect.

This bug report confirms the issue also affects **remote `hermes serve` backends** with basic auth, not just local setups.

## Workaround

Currently no workaround for non-default profiles via remote backend. Using the default profile in the Desktop App works correctly.

items.title: Memory flush agents built with skip_memory=True get a memory tool that always fails (store=None)

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: area/memory
labels.description: Memory subsystem: store, providers, sync, background reviews

items.body:
### Summary

Agents constructed with `skip_memory=True` **and** `enabled_toolsets=["memory"]` expose a memory tool that can never work: `skip_memory=True` also skips creation of the built-in file-backed `MemoryStore`, so the tool dispatcher receives `store=None` and every call returns `"Memory is not available. It may be disabled in config or this environment."` (`tools/memory_tool.py` — the `store is None` guard). The pre-compaction `flush_memories(...)` also silently no-ops at its `not self._memory_store` guard.

In v0.10.0 this made the gateway pre-reset memory flush (`_flush_memories_for_session`) a permanent no-op — the main automatic memory-capture path — while still logging `Pre-reset memory flush completed` at INFO. The same construction pattern still exists at current `main`.

### Real-world impact (v0.10.0 install, 3 months of use)

- `memory_enabled: true`, `memories/` directory empty after ~3 months / 301 sessions.
- Every memory tool call in the whole history (8 attempts) failed with the error above; the model retried saving the same user preference 3 times over 11 days (nothing persisted), then stopped attempting memory saves entirely — silent degradation.
- `agent.log` contains 13 × `Pre-reset memory flush completed for session …` with zero bytes ever written.

### Affected call sites

v0.10.0:
- `gateway/run.py` `_flush_memories_for_session` — flush agent built with `skip_memory=True  # Flush agent — no memory provider` + `enabled_toolsets=["memory", "skills"]`. The comment suggests the intent was to skip the *external provider*, but the flag also removes the built-in store.

Current `main` (checked 2026-07-16):
- `agent/agent_init.py:1377-1391` — `skip_memory=True` still skips built-in `MemoryStore` creation.
- `gateway/run.py` (~L11453, session-hygiene compaction agent) — `skip_memory=True`, `enabled_toolsets=["memory"]`.
- `gateway/slash_commands.py` (~L3232, compaction tmp agent) — `skip_memory=True`, `enabled_toolsets=["memory"]`.
- `cron/scheduler.py` (~L3198) — cron agents run `skip_memory=True`, but `_resolve_cron_disabled_toolsets` does not disable the `memory` toolset, so cron-spawned models keep attempting saves that always fail.

### Suggested fixes

Any of these (they compose):

1. When building flush/hygiene/compaction agents, attach the built-in file-backed store explicitly while keeping external providers skipped — i.e. split the meaning of `skip_memory` (e.g. `skip_memory_provider` vs `skip_memory_store`). This is the local patch we're running (v0.10.0):

```python
tmp_agent = AIAgent(..., skip_memory=True, enabled_toolsets=["memory", "skills"], ...)
# skip_memory=True keeps external memory providers out of the flush agent,
# but it also skips the built-in file-backed MemoryStore -- leaving the
# memory tool with store=None so every save fails. Attach it explicitly.
_mem_cfg = (load_config() or {}).get("memory", {})
_mem_enabled = _mem_cfg.get("memory_enabled", True)
_usr_enabled = _mem_cfg.get("user_profile_enabled", True)
if _mem_enabled or _usr_enabled:
    _store = MemoryStore(
        memory_char_limit=_mem_cfg.get("memory_char_limit", 2200),
        user_char_limit=_mem_cfg.get("user_char_limit", 1375),
    )
    _store.load_from_disk()
    tmp_agent._memory_store = _store
    tmp_agent._memory_enabled = _mem_enabled
    tmp_agent._user_profile_enabled = _usr_enabled
```

With this in place the pre-reset flush writes `memories/MEMORY.md` / `USER.md` as intended (existing gateway flush tests still pass).

2. Don't register the `memory` tool on agents whose store is `None` (gate tool exposure on store presence), and/or add `memory` to the cron always-disabled toolsets — the tool can only ever error there.

3. The `Pre-reset memory flush completed` INFO log should not claim success when the store is absent (it masked this for months).

### Repro

1. Fresh install, `memory.memory_enabled: true` (default), run the gateway.
2. Chat on any platform, then let the session hit the daily reset / idle expiry (v0.10.0), or trigger hygiene compaction on `main`.
3. `~/.hermes/memories/` is never created/written; the flush agent's transcript shows `memory` tool calls failing with `Memory is not available…`; the log still says the flush completed.

items.title: Conversation loop delivers narration text as final response when finish_reason=tool_calls (silent partial outputs in cron jobs)

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: sweeper:cannot-reproduce
labels.description: Sweeper: could not reproduce on current main

items.body:
## Summary

When an agent turn returns `finish_reason=tool_calls` alongside text content (e.g. narration like "Let me check the remaining data..."), the conversation loop can terminate the turn and deliver the **accompanying text as the final response** instead of executing the pending tool calls. This produces silent partial responses that the scheduler marks as `succeeded`, because it only validates that text was delivered — not that the task was completed.

This primarily affects autonomous/cron jobs where no user is present to notice the incomplete output and say "continue."

## Environment

- **hermes-agent**: 0.18.2 (commit `a7ef17da7a`, branch `main`)
- **Provider**: github-copilot (OpenAI-compatible chat_completions API)
- **Model**: claude-sonnet-5
- **Context**: cron job triggered via `hermes cron run <job_id>` (cron_mode: deny, no user present)

## Root cause

In `agent/conversation_loop.py`, when the model returns a message containing **both text content and tool_calls** with `finish_reason=tool_calls`, there is a code path where the turn is finalized as `text_response` and the text content is returned as `final_response` — without the tool calls being executed. The diagnostic log from `agent/turn_finalizer.py:269` confirms this:

```
Turn ended: reason=text_response(finish_reason=tool_calls) model=claude-sonnet-5
  api_calls=14/60 budget=14/60 tool_turns=13
  last_msg_role=assistant response_len=36
```

Key observations:
- `finish_reason=tool_calls` — the model requested tool execution
- `tool_turns=13` — tools were executed on calls 1-13, but **not** on the final call (#14)
- `response_len=36` — the 36-char narration text was delivered as the final response
- `last_msg_role=assistant` — not a tool result; the narration message itself was treated as the turn's output
- No `BLOCKED` messages, no errors — the tool calls were simply not executed before the turn ended

The turn exits as `text_response` even though `finish_reason` is `tool_calls`, which is contradictory: if the model emitted tool calls, the loop should either execute them or retry — not deliver the accompanying text as a final response.

## Reproduction

1. Configure a cron job with a multi-step scan prompt (e.g. a security audit that runs ~15 terminal commands in sequence).
2. Trigger it: `hermes cron run <job_id> --accept-hooks`
3. The model will execute tools for several turns, then eventually emit a message with narration text + tool_calls. The loop terminates and delivers the narration as the final response.

This is **non-deterministic**: the same job with the same prompt succeeds ~25% of the time (when the model happens to not narrate mid-scan) and fails ~75% of the time (when it does).

## Evidence (4 runs, same job, same prompt)

| Run | Session ID | finish_reason | tool_turns | response_len | Result |
|-----|-----------|---------------|------------|--------------|--------|
| 1 (08:15) | `cron_6867160772ca_20260716_081532` | `tool_calls` | 9 | 127 chars | ❌ Narration delivered as report |
| 2 (08:20) | `cron_6867160772ca_20260716_082008` | `stop` | 5 | 5138 chars | ✅ Full report |
| 3 (08:33) | `cron_6867160772ca_20260716_083351` | `tool_calls` | 12 | 80 chars | ❌ Narration delivered as report |
| 4 (08:51) | `cron_6867160772ca_20260716_085128` | `tool_calls` | 13 | 36 chars | ❌ Narration delivered as report |

Run 2 is the only success — it ended with `finish_reason=stop` (the model produced the final report as pure text, no pending tool calls). The three failures all ended with `finish_reason=tool_calls` but were treated as `text_response` exits.

The failed responses were short narration fragments:
- Run 1: "Bon, TLS1.0 rejeté, TLS1.2 accepté = sain. Récupérons les dernières données : git ls-files, cron, journaux/IOC, SSH keys count."
- Run 3: "Bien, TLS1.0 rejeté, TLS1.2 accepté. Voyons le reste (cron, git, journaux, IOC)."
- Run 4: "TLS1.0 rejeté, TLS1.2 accepté — bon."

All three were delivered to the user (Telegram) as if they were the completed report, and the scheduler marked `last_status: ok`.

## Expected behavior

When `finish_reason=tool_calls`:
- The tool calls **should be executed**, and the loop should continue to the next iteration.
- If the tool calls cannot be executed (e.g. all blocked by approval policy), the loop should **retry or return an error**, not deliver the accompanying text as a final response.
- A turn should only exit as `text_response` when `finish_reason=stop` (or `length` after continuation attempts), meaning the model intentionally ended with a text-only response.

## Actual behavior

When `finish_reason=tool_calls` and the message contains text + tool_calls:
- The text content is returned as `final_response`
- The tool calls are silently dropped
- The turn exits as `text_response(finish_reason=tool_calls)` — a contradictory state
- The scheduler marks the job as `succeeded`
- The user receives a partial/narration response as if it were the completed output

## Impact

- **Silent data loss**: autonomous jobs (cron, background tasks) produce incomplete outputs that are marked as successful. No user is present to notice and retry.
- **Security pipeline reliability**: our biweekly security audit pipeline delivers partial reports ~75% of the time, with no indication of failure.
- **Cost waste**: each failed run costs ~$0.20 (model API calls for 14 turns of work, none of which appears in the final output).
- **Non-deterministic**: the same job succeeds or fails based on whether the model happens to narrate mid-scan, making it impossible to reliably test or validate.

## Possible fix

In the turn finalization logic, when `finish_reason=tool_calls`:
- Do not accept the turn as a `text_response` exit.
- Either execute the pending tool calls and continue the loop, or if execution is not possible, return a `partial=True` result with an error explaining that tool calls were not executed.
- Only treat a turn as a completed `text_response` when `finish_reason` is `stop` (genuine end-of-response) or `length` (after continuation attempts are exhausted).

## Workaround attempted

We tried instructing the model via prompt to never produce narration text between tool calls ("un tour intermédiaire ne doit contenir QUE des appels d'outils — aucun contenu texte"). This did not resolve the issue — the model (claude-sonnet-5) continues to narrate mid-scan despite explicit instructions, and the loop delivers the narration as the final response.

items.title: feat(plugins): public subagent lifecycle API — launch/monitor/cancel child sessions from plugins

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

items.body:
## Summary

Give plugins a sanctioned, typed service for launching, monitoring, canceling, and retrieving results from Hermes child sessions (subagents) — `ctx.subagent_lifecycle` — instead of importing `tools/delegate_tool.py` internals or shelling out to `hermes chat`.

Part of the plugin-interface expansion tracking issue #64182. Added in round-3 review.

## Motivation

- @asimons81 shipped PR #63359 implementing exactly this surface, with a stated downstream consumer (hardproof — plugin-driven subagent orchestration) blocked on it.
- Plugins that want to fan work out to child sessions today have no public path: `delegate_task` is a model tool (agent-invoked, not plugin-invoked), and the delegation runtime in `tools/delegate_tool.py` is internal surface that can change any release.
- The event bus (#64164) and gateway injection (#61096) both make "a plugin reacts to an external event by spawning bounded agent work" a realistic pattern; that pattern needs a supervised child-session primitive or plugins will hand-roll it badly.

## Current state

- `tools/delegate_tool.py` owns child spawning, concurrency caps (`delegation.max_concurrent_children`), depth limits, and the async completion queue — all reachable only through the model-tool path.
- `hermes_cli/plugins.py` `PluginContext` has no delegation/subagent surface.
- No isolation story exists for "which plugin owns which child" — nothing prevents a plugin from observing or canceling children it didn't launch, because there is no plugin-facing handle at all.

## Proposed shape (additive)

```python
svc = ctx.subagent_lifecycle          # typed service, capability-gated
handle = svc.launch(goal=..., context=..., toolsets=[...])
svc.status(handle)                    # queued / running / done / failed / canceled
svc.cancel(handle)                    # cooperative cancellation
svc.result(handle)                    # bounded retention, then evicted
```

Contract points (several already implemented in #63359 — review against these, don't re-derive):

- **Capability-gated, default off** — `plugins.entries.<id>.allow_subagents: true` (folds into the #64228 declared-capability model when that lands).
- **Cross-parent isolation** — handles are unforgeable (#63359 uses HMAC-capability handles); a plugin can only see/cancel children it launched.
- **Core floors are not bypassable** — child spawns count against `delegation.max_concurrent_children` / `max_spawn_depth` exactly like model-tool delegations; the plugin path must not be a second, uncapped spawn lane.
- **Bounded result retention** — results are evicted after a cap; no unbounded growth.
- **Lifecycle integration** — launched children become ledger entries under #64229: plugin unload/reload cancels its children (or explicitly detaches with a documented policy), so force-reload can't orphan running subagents.

## Backward compatibility

Additive `PluginContext` property; no change to `delegate_task`, existing plugins, or the delegation config surface.

## Security considerations

- Default off per plugin; enabling is an explicit config grant.
- Subagents launched by plugins get the same toolset restrictions and approval machinery as model-launched children — no privilege escalation via the plugin path.
- Handles must not be guessable or transferable across plugin boundaries.

## Salvage candidate

PR #63359 (@asimons81) — 650+ additions, tests, docs, CI green per author. Review notes for salvage:

- It touches core files (`run_agent.py`, `tools/delegate_tool.py`, `hermes_cli/plugins.py`) — expected for a host-owned primitive, but the diff needs the standard footprint review: the core hook points should be minimal and the service logic should live in its own module (`agent/subagent_lifecycle.py` in the PR).
- Verify the concurrency/depth floors above are enforced through the *existing* delegation limits, not a parallel accounting.
- Re-review the unload/cancellation story once #64229's ledger lands; if #63359 merges first, wiring children into the ledger becomes a #64229 acceptance criterion.

## Relationship

- Depends on (or co-designs with) #64229 — supervised cleanup on unload.
- Capability grant unifies into #64228 when that lands.
- Complements #64164 (event-driven plugins that spawn work) and #61096 (gateway injection — the "notify the user" half of the same automation patterns).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `ctx.subagent_lifecycle` gated behind a default-off per-plugin config grant
- [ ] Launch/status/cancel/result round-trip covered by contract tests, including cross-parent isolation (plugin B cannot touch plugin A's children)
- [ ] Child spawns provably bounded by `delegation.max_concurrent_children` and `max_spawn_depth` shared with the model-tool path (test that mixed plugin+model spawning hits one shared cap)
- [ ] Plugin unload cancels (or documented-policy-detaches) its children; no orphaned children after force-reload
- [ ] Result retention bounded; eviction tested
- [ ] Docs page in the developer guide; #63359 salvaged with contributor credit if the design review passes

items.title: feat(plugins): gateway-session message injection — ctx.inject_message(session_key=...)

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state

labels.name: sweeper:risk-message-delivery
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may drop, duplicate, misroute, or suppress messages

items.body:
## Summary

Let a plugin trigger a conversational turn in an existing, live **gateway** session — the exact Telegram/Discord/Slack/WhatsApp thread the user is already talking in — via an additive keyword on the existing primitive: `ctx.inject_message(content, session_key=...)`. Today `inject_message` is CLI-only.

Part of the plugin-interface expansion tracking issue #64182. Added in round-3 review. Covers #59263 and the plugin-facing half of #61096.

## Motivation

- #59263 / #61096: external processes (webhook daemons, monitors, cron, other agent runs) cannot wake the agent inside the user's existing gateway DM with full conversation history. `hermes chat --resume` cannot resolve gateway session keys; `hermes webhook subscribe` always starts a new disconnected session; the only fallback is a one-way "pager" curl to the platform API.
- @GodsBoy reviewed the tracker and implemented exactly this slice as PR #64436 rather than filing another overlapping proposal — monitors, reminders, external event consumers, and security layers all need "notify the user in-thread and let the agent react."
- This boundary belongs in core: Hermes owns session identity, authorization, queueing, and platform delivery. Plugins should request a turn through a narrow host-owned primitive, not import gateway internals or talk to platform SDKs directly.

## Current state

- `PluginContext.inject_message()` (`hermes_cli/plugins.py` ~L476) queues into the CLI's `_pending_input`/`_interrupt_queue`; in gateway mode it logs a warning and returns False.
- Gateway sessions live in `gateway_routing` keyed `agent:main:<platform>:<chat_type>:<chat_id>`; there is no plugin-reachable path to them.

## Proposed shape (additive)

```python
ctx.inject_message("MR #42 merged — verify and continue", session_key="agent:main:telegram:dm:12345")
```

Contract points (largely implemented in salvage candidate #64436 — review against these):

- **Default off per plugin** — explicit config grant (`plugins.entries.<id>.allow_gateway_inject: true` or equivalent); folds into #64228's capability model when that lands.
- **Existing persisted sessions only** — no session creation, rotation, or resurrection through this path.
- **Authorization revalidated at dispatch time** — not inherited from stale adapter-time decisions.
- **Non-control input** — plugin payloads cannot invoke slash commands, approval responses, or any human gateway control; security metadata preserved through busy-session queueing.
- **Alternation-safe** — injection enters as a normal user-turn through the existing queue/interrupt machinery; no synthetic mid-loop messages (system-prompt/message-flow invariants hold).
- **Honest return value** — `True` means the gateway accepted asynchronous dispatch, not that the turn or platform delivery completed.

## Out of scope (stays with sibling issues)

Target discovery API, rich message envelopes, delivery receipts, public HTTP endpoint, policy middleware — #61096 (broader external-event surface), #64176 (platform actions), #64228 (capabilities), #64231 (hook taxonomy).

## Backward compatibility

Keyword-only addition; CLI call shape and behavior unchanged. Old plugins unaffected.

## Security considerations

- Fail closed: no grant → gateway targeting refused, logged.
- A plugin can only reach sessions the host resolves for it under current authorization; no ambient authority over every chat.
- Injected turns run with the session's normal toolsets and approval machinery — this is a message, not an execution bypass.

## Salvage candidate

PR #64436 (@GodsBoy) — implements the slice above with per-plugin grant, authz revalidation, non-control payload handling, FIFO separation for mixed user/plugin follow-ups, tests, and docs. CI green per author. Review notes: the diff touches `gateway/run.py`, `gateway/session.py`, `gateway/platforms/base.py`, `gateway/authz_mixin.py` — needs the standard two-message-guard audit (base adapter queue + runner intercept) and confirmation the scheduler registration cleans up on shutdown/reload (ties into #64229's ledger).

## Relationship

- Fixes #59263; delivers the plugin-facing half of #61096.
- Grant model unifies into #64228; scheduler/lifecycle cleanup ties into #64229.
- Complements #64164 (event bus): "external event → plugin → wake the user's thread" becomes a fully sanctioned pattern.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `inject_message(session_key=...)` works against a live gateway session on at least two platforms (E2E, not mocked adapters)
- [ ] Default-off grant enforced; ungated plugins get a logged refusal
- [ ] Cannot create/resurrect sessions; cannot invoke slash commands or approval controls via injected content (negative tests)
- [ ] Authorization revalidated at dispatch; revoked users/chats are refused
- [ ] Busy-session behavior: injection queues without corrupting message-role alternation; mixed user+plugin follow-ups preserve order and metadata
- [ ] CLI behavior byte-identical when `session_key` omitted
- [ ] #64436 salvaged with contributor credit if design review passes

items.title: feat(plugins): additive-only redaction pattern registry — ctx.register_redaction_patterns()

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

items.body:
## Summary

Let plugins register **additive-only** secret-redaction patterns — `ctx.register_redaction_patterns()` — so vendor token formats missing from core (internal PKI formats, niche SaaS keys, org-specific credential shapes) get redacted from tool output, logs, and displays without a core PR per vendor.

Part of the plugin-interface expansion tracking issue #64182. Added in round-3 review.

## Motivation

- @webdevtodayjason built this as PR #58550 alongside the #58524 hook work and asked for an explicit disposition on the tracker rather than letting it float.
- Core's `_PREFIX_PATTERNS` in `agent/redact.py` can never enumerate every vendor's token format; today the only fix for an unrecognized format is a core PR. A registry makes redaction coverage extensible the same way `register_secret_source()` made secret *retrieval* extensible — it's a ctx registry in that family, not a hook, which is why it doesn't fit the #64231 cluster.

## Current state

- `agent/redact.py`: `_PREFIX_PATTERNS` + `_PREFIX_SUBSTRINGS` literal pre-screen (derived at module load so new patterns can't silently break the fast path), `redact_sensitive_text()`, `redact_terminal_output()`.
- No plugin surface touches redaction at all.

## Proposed shape (additive)

```python
ctx.register_redaction_patterns([
    r"nvapi-[A-Za-z0-9_-]{20,}",
])
```

Structural safety properties (as designed in #58550 — these are the review bar, keep them):

- **Over-redact only, never expose.** No API exists to remove, replace, or weaken a built-in pattern. The worst a malicious/buggy plugin can do is redact too much.
- **Patterns must compile** — invalid regex is rejected at registration with a logged error, plugin load continues.
- **≥2 leading literal characters required** — keeps the `_PREFIX_SUBSTRINGS` pre-screen effective (plugin literals join the derived tuple) and makes redact-everything patterns like `.*` structurally impossible.
- **ReDoS bound** — registration should reject patterns with pathological constructs or enforce a match-time budget; a plugin pattern must not be able to stall the redaction hot path that wraps every terminal output.

## Backward compatibility

Zero behavior change when unused; core patterns untouched.

## Security considerations

- Additive-only by construction (see above) — this surface satisfies ground rule 4 without a config gate for the base capability, since the failure mode is over-redaction, not exposure. Whether it should still appear as a *declared* capability for consent visibility is a #64228 question, not a blocker here.
- Registrations become ledger entries under #64229: unload removes a plugin's patterns and rebuilds the pre-screen tuple.

## Salvage candidate

PR #58550 (@webdevtodayjason) — registry + validation + tests + an opt-in reference plugin (`nvapi-redaction`) covering a real format missing from core. CI green per author. Review notes: confirm the pre-screen tuple is rebuilt (not bypassed) when plugin patterns register after module load, and add the unload path once #64229 lands.

## Relationship

- Registry sibling of `register_secret_source()` (#64177 family).
- Ledger cleanup via #64229; optional capability declaration via #64228.
- The companion docs PR #58538 routes to #64230 (author-guide track), not here.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `ctx.register_redaction_patterns()` with compile validation, ≥2-literal-prefix rule, and rejection logging

items.title: Gateway session lists can hide same-chat history on busy platforms

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

items.body:
## Bug Description

Gateway `/sessions` and bare `/resume` can hide valid same-chat history on a busy Telegram installation. Sessions and reset boundaries are present in `state.db`, but unrelated Telegram chats and topics consume the fixed database result window before the gateway applies exact-origin visibility checks.

This is a listing-order defect, not lost history or a failed automatic reset.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Create several titled sessions in one Telegram DM lane.
2. Create more than 10 newer titled Telegram sessions under other DM or topic `session_key` values.
3. Run `/sessions` or bare `/resume` from the original DM.
4. Compare the response with an exact `session_key` query against `SessionDB.list_sessions_rich`.

A deterministic test fixture with 60 newer foreign Telegram lanes reproduces the failure on current `main`.

## Expected Behavior

The database should select candidates from the caller's exact deterministic lane before applying the SQL result limit. Compression continuations should remain one logical result, current-session exclusion should remain unchanged, and the existing gateway IDOR checks should still validate every returned row.

## Actual Behavior

The current path selects a limited platform-wide page first, then projects compression chains and applies `_resume_row_visible`. On a busy installation, the platform-wide page can contain almost entirely unrelated lanes, leaving no useful same-chat rows after visibility filtering.

## Affected Component

- Gateway session listing and resume
- Telegram confirmed, with the same query-order risk on other multi-lane gateway platforms

## Environment

- Linux 6.8, x86_64
- Python 3.11.14
- Installed Hermes Agent v0.18.2 (2026.7.7.2)
- Current `main` also reproduces with an isolated temporary SQLite fixture

## Anonymised Live Evidence

A read-only inspection of one affected Telegram DM found:

- 77 physical session rows
- 15 listable logical roots
- valid source, chat, user, thread, and `session_key` metadata on recent rows
- automatic reset and compression boundaries present
- plain `/sessions`: 10 platform-wide SQL candidates became 1 visible same-DM row
- bare `/resume`: 10 platform-wide SQL candidates became 2 visible same-DM rows, including the current conversation
- an exact-lane query returned 10 useful prior logical conversations

No message contents, titles, chat IDs, user IDs, session IDs, database copies, or raw logs are attached. A public debug-share link was intentionally not generated because it would expose private session metadata; the synthetic reproduction covers the same code path.

## Root Cause Analysis

`SessionDB.list_sessions_rich` supports source filtering and applies `LIMIT` in SQL. The gateway then runs compression projection, deduplication, current-session exclusion, and origin visibility checks. Because the query has no exact lane predicate, unrelated rows from the same platform can consume the page before those later checks.

There is a related compression edge case: an authorised cross-lane `/resume` rebinds a compression tip to the destination lane. The root and tip must retain one routing peer, otherwise an exact root predicate can make that logical conversation disappear from ordinary destination-lane lists later.

## Proposed Fix

1. Add an optional parameterised `session_key` predicate to `SessionDB.list_sessions_rich`, applied before ordering and `LIMIT`.
2. Thread it through the shared session-listing helper.
3. Use the normalised runtime source for `/sessions` and bare or numeric-fallback `/resume`.
4. Omit the key only for the existing, explicitly authenticated admin widening paths.
5. Keep `_resume_row_visible` and `_resume_target_allowed` unchanged as defence in depth.
6. When the existing explicit switch moves a compression tip, update its compression ancestors in the same bounded routing write so the logical lineage keeps one key.

This avoids an arbitrary larger over-fetch window, uses the existing `idx_sessions_session_key` index, performs no migration or background backfill, and does not weaken origin isolation.

## Related Work, Not Duplicates

- #54326 and its related PRs address current-session indexing for numeric `/resume`, not source-wide candidate starvation.
- #60138 remembers numbered `/sessions search` choices, but does not change the database candidate population.
- #62138 adds the same optional database primitive for model-facing `session_search`; it does not fix gateway `/sessions` or bare `/resume`. The implementation should rebase away the shared hunk if that PR lands first.
- #62278 carries origin metadata into compression and branch children. It improves metadata creation but does not move gateway list limiting behind exact-lane selection.

## Regression Coverage

The fix should cover more than 50 foreign same-platform lanes, reset roots, current compressed-tip exclusion, full and search modes, bare and numeric resume, Telegram topic recovery, admin and non-admin widening, cross-origin blocking, null-key fail-closed behavior, indexed query planning, and cross-lane compressed-session switching.

I have a focused implementation and am willing to submit the PR.

items.title: Desktop UI model pill is disabled after session starts — canSwitch gated on gatewayOpen instead of session state

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
##Environment

Windows 10
Hermes Desktop v0.1.82 (+17)
Provider: moa (Mixture of Agents preset-based routing)

##Summary

After a conversation session is established, the model pill (model selector button) in the composer area becomes permanently disabled, preventing users from switching models mid-session — even when the agent is idle and waiting for the next instruction.

The root cause is that `canSwitch` on the model pill is hardwired to `gatewayOpen` (`gatewayState === 'open'`), which does not account for active session state. Once a session is live, the user cannot switch models through the UI at all.

Root Cause — Key Code Chain

 #1. Model pill `canSwitch` is gated on gateway state

File: `apps/desktop/src/app/chat/index.tsx` (line 348)

typescript
canSwitch: gatewayOpen,

And the entire ChatBar is also disabled when the gateway is not open:

disabled={!gatewayOpen},  // line 505

Where gatewayOpen is derived from:

const gatewayState = useStore($gatewayState)       // line 260
const gatewayOpen = gatewayState === 'open'          // line 262

#2. Live session owns the model state — initialization skips
File: apps/desktop/src/app/session/hooks/use-model-controls.ts (lines 43–47)

const refreshCurrentModel = useCallback(async (force = false) => {
    try {
      if ($activeSessionId.get()) {
        return  // ← exits early when a session is active
      }

This means once a session is created, the model selection is "owned" by the session and the UI's model init logic deliberately skips updating it. The comment says: "A live session owns the footer, so skip entirely."

3. MoA (Mixture of Agents) presets complicate switching further
When using the moa provider, the "model" is actually a preset name (e.g., 日常对话-高峰) that maps to a configuration of reference models + aggregator model. Switching from a MoA preset to a different model type mid-session would require re-initializing the entire agent runtime, which is architecturally challenging.

File: hermes_cli/model_switch.py — MoA presets are resolved via exact_moa_preset_name() and normalize_moa_config(), but the desktop UI's model selector completely bypasses this path when gatewayOpen is false.

Why This Is a Problem
The /model slash command does work when typed manually in the chat input — it routes through the gateway RPC (config.set with --session flag) and is not blocked. However, the graphical model pill in the desktop UI is disabled, creating a poor UX where:

Users cannot discover that model switching is possible via /model
The UI provides no feedback about why the model pill is disabled
After a gateway reconnect or session recovery, the model pill remains locked even though the agent is fully responsive
Suggested Fix
The canSwitch property should account for session state, not just gateway state. A possible approach:

canSwitch: gatewayOpen || !!activeSessionId,


This would keep the model pill disabled while the gateway is connecting (preventing errors), but enable it once either:
- The gateway is fully open, OR
- An active session exists (even if the gateway state is ambiguous)

Additionally, the MoA preset switching path should be surfaced in the desktop model picker so users can switch between MoA presets mid-session without needing to type `/model` manually.

## Workaround

Users can still switch models by typing `/model <model-name>` (e.g., `/model deepseek-v4-pro`) directly into the chat input — this bypasses the UI restriction and routes through the gateway RPC.

items.title: Three sites use subprocess with shell=True on untrusted or user-influenced input

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

labels.name: sweeper:cannot-reproduce
labels.description: Sweeper: could not reproduce on current main

items.body:
Three locations in the codebase pass untrusted or user-influenced strings to `subprocess.run(..., shell=True)`. `shell=True` causes the command string to be parsed by the shell, enabling metacharacter injection if any interpolated value is attacker-controlled.

---

**Site 1 — `hermes_cli/mcp_catalog.py:367`**

**Context:** `_run_bootstrap_commands()` runs commands from an MCP catalog entry's `bootstrap` field. These entries are loaded from user-managed JSON (`mcp-catalog.json`).

**Current code:**
python
for cmd in commands:
    proc = subprocess.run(cmd, cwd=str(cwd), shell=True)
**Risk:** `cmd` is a raw string from the catalog JSON. A malicious catalog entry can inject shell metacharacters.

**Suggested fix:** If `cmd` is always a simple single command, use `subprocess.run(shlex.split(cmd), cwd=str(cwd))`. If `&&` / `||` chaining is required, parse the command safely or require a list-of-strings format in the catalog schema.

---

**Site 2 — `hermes_cli/web_server.py:4646`**

**Context:** Plugin install handler runs `npm install` / `pip install` strings from third-party plugin manifests.

**Current code:**
python
install = _run_setup_command(
    install_cmd,
    display=install_cmd,
    shell=True,
    timeout=300,
)
**Risk:** `install_cmd` comes from a plugin's `plugin.yaml` or manifest. A malicious plugin can inject via shell metacharacters.

**Suggested fix:** For `npm install` and `pip install` specifically, split into list form (`["npm", "install"]` or `["pip", "install", "-r", "requirements.txt"]`) instead of shell strings. The `_run_setup_command()` helper should accept a list and pass it without `shell=True`.

---

**Site 3 — `tools/transcription_tools.py:1237`**

**Context:** Local STT command runs a user-provided template string.

**Current code:**
python 
use_shell = bool(os.getenv(LOCAL_STT_COMMAND_ENV, "").strip())
if use_shell:
    subprocess.run(command, shell=True, ...)
**Risk:** `command` is built from a template string supplied via `LOCAL_STT_COMMAND_ENV`. While individual interpolated values are `shlex.quote()`-wrapped before formatting, the template itself is executed via `shell=True`. A malicious template (e.g., `"; rm -rf /; #`) executes arbitrary code.

**Suggested fix:** Always use `shlex.split(command)` and pass as a list to `subprocess.run()` without `shell=True`. If the template genuinely needs shell features, document the requirement and validate the template against an allowlist of safe patterns.

---

**Severity:** Medium-to-High — all three require the attacker to control a catalog entry, plugin manifest, or env var respectively, but the blast radius is arbitrary code execution in the Hermes process context.

items.title: prompt_toolkit crashes with NoConsoleScreenBufferError on Windows when `hermes chat -q` stdout is piped (non-interactive/automated use)

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

labels.name: sweeper:risk-platform-windows
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break or behave differently on native Windows

items.body:
### Summary

On Windows, `hermes chat -q "<prompt>"` crashes with `prompt_toolkit.output.win32.NoConsoleScreenBufferError: No Windows console found. Are you running cmd.exe?` whenever Hermes' stdout is **not a real console** — e.g. when it is spawned by another process with `stdio: pipe` (any automation/orchestration tool, CI, or programmatic integration). This makes the documented "single query (non-interactive mode)" flag unusable from any Windows automation context, since capturing the response text inherently requires piping stdout.

### Environment

- Hermes Agent v0.10.0 (2026.4.16, upstream `4a69a662`)
- Windows (child process spawned via Node.js `child_process.spawn` with `stdio: ['ignore','pipe','pipe']`, `shell: false`)
- `prompt_toolkit` output backend selection

### Steps to reproduce

Spawn Hermes as a non-console child process (this is exactly what any orchestrator/automation wrapper does to capture output):

```js
const { spawn } = require('child_process');
const child = spawn('hermes', ['chat', '-q', 'Reply with exactly the single word: PONG', '-Q'], {
  stdio: ['ignore', 'pipe', 'pipe'],
  shell: false,
});
```

or equivalently from a shell with stdout redirected to a pipe/file rather than a terminal:

```powershell
hermes chat -q "Reply with exactly the single word: PONG" -Q | Out-File out.txt
```

### Actual result

Exit code 1, no query response, and (without `-Q`, or in some `-Q` cases too) a traceback ending in:

```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  ...
  File "...\hermes-agent\cli.py", line 8321, in chat
    _cprint(f"{_DIM}Initializing agent...{_RST}")
  File "...\hermes-agent\cli.py", line 1254, in _cprint
    _pt_print(_PT_ANSI(text))
  File "...\prompt_toolkit\shortcuts\utils.py", line 111, in print_formatted_text
    output = get_app_session().output
  File "...\prompt_toolkit\application\current.py", line 67, in output
    self._output = create_output()
  File "...\prompt_toolkit\output\defaults.py", line 91, in create_output
    return Win32Output(stdout, default_color_depth=color_depth_from_env)
  File "...\prompt_toolkit\output\win32.py", line 115, in __init__
    info = self.get_win32_screen_buffer_info()
  File "...\prompt_toolkit\output\win32.py", line 219, in get_win32_screen_buffer_info
    raise NoConsoleScreenBufferError
prompt_toolkit.output.win32.NoConsoleScreenBufferError: No Windows console found. Are you running cmd.exe?
```

Separately, without forcing `PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8` in the child environment, the banner/spinner rendering (box-drawing + braille characters) also raises `UnicodeEncodeError: 'charmap' codec can't encode characters ...` when stdout falls back to the default Windows console codepage (cp1252) instead of UTF-8 — a second, related issue with the same root cause (assuming a real interactive console is always present).

### Root cause

`prompt_toolkit/output/defaults.py::create_output()` has this branch on `sys.platform == "win32"`:

```python
if sys.platform == "win32":
    if is_win_vt100_enabled():
        return Windows10_Output(...)
    if is_conemu_ansi():
        return ConEmuOutput(...)
    else:
        return Win32Output(stdout, default_color_depth=color_depth_from_env)
```

Unlike the POSIX branch just below it (which checks `stdout.isatty()` and falls back to `PlainTextOutput` when stdout is not a terminal), the Windows branch has **no such fallback** — it unconditionally tries `Win32Output`, which calls `GetConsoleScreenBufferInfo` on the process's `STD_OUTPUT_HANDLE`. When that handle is a pipe (not a console), the Win32 API call fails and `Win32Output.__init__` raises `NoConsoleScreenBufferError` with no graceful degradation path.

This means **any non-interactive/automated invocation of Hermes on Windows is currently broken**, since capturing output for programmatic use always requires `stdio: pipe`.

### Suggested fix

Either (or both):

1. In Hermes' own `cli.py` `_cprint`, catch `prompt_toolkit.output.win32.NoConsoleScreenBufferError` (and ideally check `sys.stdout.isatty()` up front) and fall back to plain `print()` when no real console is attached — mirrors what `prompt_toolkit` already does correctly on POSIX.
2. Upstream in `prompt_toolkit` itself: add an `isatty()`/pipe check to the `win32` branch of `create_output()` (parity with the POSIX branch), returning `PlainTextOutput` when stdout isn't a real console, instead of unconditionally requiring `Win32Output`'s console-buffer query to succeed.

### Workaround

Set `PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8` in the child environment to avoid the separate charmap crash on the banner text, and use `-Q` (quiet mode) to suppress most `_cprint` calls — but this does **not** fully avoid the `NoConsoleScreenBufferError` path for every non-interactive invocation on Windows, since some `_cprint` calls still fire under `-q`/`-Q` (e.g. the "Initializing agent..." message) whenever there's no attached console at all.

Happy to test a fix against a real automation harness if useful — this was found while wiring Hermes up as a pluggable local LLM backend in an orchestration tool and confirmed via a minimal repro spawning `hermes.exe` directly with `stdio: pipe`, isolating it from any surrounding tooling.

items.title: Regression: TUI injects NODE_ENV=production → hermes update web UI build fails (tsc not found) on main

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

labels.name: sweeper:risk-compatibility
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break existing users, config, migrations, defaults, or upgrades

labels.name: comp/dashboard
labels.description: Web dashboard / control panel UI (dashboard/, landing)

items.body:
## Summary

`hermes update` still fails the web UI build on current `main` with:

```text
> web@0.0.0 build
> tsc -b && vite build
sh: 1: tsc: not found
⚠ Web UI build failed — serving stale dist as fallback
```

Root cause is unchanged from #27430: `NODE_ENV=production` makes npm omit `devDependencies`, and `typescript` / `vite` live under `web` **devDependencies**. The new angle is **Hermes itself injects `NODE_ENV=production` for the default TUI path**, so this is not limited to VPS/CI shells that happen to export production.

#27430 was closed as completed (2026-06-30) but the install/build path on current main still does not force `--include=dev` or strip `NODE_ENV`. Several fix PRs remain open and unmerged.

## Self-injection path (not just external env)

Default non-dev TUI launch sets production NODE_ENV:

```python
# hermes_cli/main.py ~2038
env.setdefault("NODE_ENV", "development" if tui_dev else "production")
```

Process tree observed on a live WSL git install after update:

| Process | NODE_ENV |
|---|---|
| `hermes` CLI parent | unset |
| `ui-tui/dist/entry.js` | **production** |
| `tui_gateway.entry` | **production** |
| agent terminal / `hermes update` children | **production** (inherited) |

So a user who never put `NODE_ENV=production` in `.bashrc` still hits this every time they update **from TUI / agent**.

`_build_web_ui` then builds its npm env from `with_hermes_node_path()` (copies process env) and runs install + build without neutralizing that:

```python
# hermes_cli/main.py ~4907-4955
build_env = with_hermes_node_path()  # inherits NODE_ENV=production
r1 = _run_npm_install_deterministic(
    npm, npm_cwd,
    extra_args=(*npm_workspace_args, "--silent"),
    env=build_env,
)
r2 = _run_with_idle_timeout([npm, "run", "build"], cwd=web_dir, env=build_env)
```

`_update_node_dependencies()` has the same inheritance for the ui-tui + web workspace install step.

## Local verification (current main)

```text
Hermes: v0.18.2 · HEAD e844ea9f
Node: v24.15.0 · npm 11.18.0
OS: WSL2 Ubuntu
```

```bash
# inherited from TUI agent session
echo $NODE_ENV                    # production
npm config get omit               # ["dev"]

# web package pins build tools as devDeps only
# web/package.json: "build": "tsc -b && vite build"
#                   "devDependencies": { "typescript": "^6.0.3", "vite": "^8.0.16", ... }

# after production-scoped install:
test -e node_modules/.bin/tsc || echo NO_tsc   # NO_tsc

# repro:
NODE_ENV=production npm ci --workspace web --silent
# → typescript stripped again

# fix (local):
env -u NODE_ENV npm install --workspace web --include=dev
env -u NODE_ENV npm run build -w web
# → tsc present, vite build succeeds (~1.3s, 488 modules)
```

`~/.hermes/logs/update.log` shows the same failure block with the soft stale-dist fallback (by design from #23817), so updates look successful while the dashboard remains on old assets.

## Why this keeps recurring

1. TUI (or dashboard) injects `NODE_ENV=production` for React runtime — correct for **serving**, wrong for **npm install of build tools**.
2. That env bleeds into update/build subprocesses.
3. Soft fallback hides the failure; no hard signal that dashboard is stale.
4. Next TUI-driven `hermes update` re-runs production-scoped install and can strip `tsc` again even after a manual repair.

## Suggested direction

Fix at the **npm subprocess boundary** (not by asking users to unset env):

1. In `_build_web_ui` and `_update_node_dependencies` / `_run_npm_install_deterministic` when building web/ui-tui:
   - `build_env.pop("NODE_ENV", None)`, **or**
   - always pass `--include=dev` for those workspace installs.
2. Keep `NODE_ENV=production` for the actual TUI/dashboard **runtime** process; only neutralize it for install/build.
3. Optionally log when omit/dev stripping would have applied, so stale-dist fallback is less silent.

Existing open fix PRs already sketch this (none on main yet):

- #25649 — strip `NODE_ENV` from npm subprocess  
- #17906 / #18682 — force `NODE_ENV=development` around web build  
- #22187 — `--include=dev` for web UI  
- #38416 — desktop rebuild `--include=dev`

## Related

- #27430 (closed completed, but behavior still present on main)  
- #49920 (desktop CONNECTING hang; marked duplicate of #27430 — same root cause)  
- Soft fallback context: #23817  

## Workaround

```bash
env -u NODE_ENV hermes update
# or after a failed update:
cd ~/.hermes/hermes-agent
env -u NODE_ENV npm install --workspace web --include=dev --no-fund --no-audit
env -u NODE_ENV npm run build -w web
```

Happy to test a preferred variant of the four open fix PRs against this TUI-inheritance repro if useful.

items.title: Ollama Cloud "session usage limit" 429 error not triggering fallback_providers chain

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: sweeper:cannot-reproduce
labels.description: Sweeper: could not reproduce on current main

items.body:
Bug: Ollama Cloud "session usage limit" 429 error not recognised as quota exhaustion — fallback_providers chain never triggered

### Summary

When Ollama Cloud returns an HTTP 429 with the error message `"you (robbos_ai_world) have reached your session usage limit, upgrade for higher limits"`, Hermes treats it as a **transient rate limit**, retries the same provider 3 times, then gives up with "Final error" — but **never triggers the `fallback_providers` chain**.

Per the [Fallback Providers docs](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/features/fallback-providers#provider-quota-errors-that-trigger-fallback), quota exhaustion should trigger the fallback ladder. The docs explicitly say:

> If your provider returns a different phrase for daily-quota exhaustion and Hermes doesn't trigger fallback, that's a bug — open an issue with the exact error string.

The Ollama Cloud error string `"session usage limit"` / `"upgrade for higher limits"` is not in Hermes's quota-exhaustion keyword list, so it's misclassified as a transient rate limit instead of quota exhaustion.

### Environment

- **Hermes Agent:** v0.18.0 (2026.7.1)
- **OS:** macOS (Mac mini Pro M4 Pro)
- **Primary model:** `glm-5.2:cloud` on provider `ollama-jetson` (Jetson Orin Nano)
- **Fallback chain:** `ollama/gemma4:31b-mlx` (Mac local) → `ollama-jetson/gpt-oss:120b-cloud` (Jetson cloud) → `ollama/nemotron3:33b` (Mac local)

### The error from gateway logs

```
HTTP 429: {"error":"you (#########) have reached your session usage limit, upgrade for higher limits: https://ollama.com/upgrade or add extra usage: https://ollama.com/settings"}
```

### Behaviour observed

1. Hermes retries the same provider 3 times (attempts 1/3, 2/3, 3/3)
2. After 3 retries, logs `"Rate limited after 3 retries"` and `"Final error"`
3. `fallback_providers` chain is **never triggered**
4. The user has working local Ollama models on a separate machine (Mac) that would respond fine, but they're never reached

### Expected behaviour

The Ollama Cloud error string `"session usage limit"` / `"upgrade for higher limits"` should be recognised as **quota exhaustion** (not transient rate limiting) and trigger the `fallback_providers` chain automatically.

Per the docs, Hermes currently recognises these quota-exhaustion phrases:

- Bedrock / LiteLLM: `Too many tokens per day`, `daily limit`, `tokens per day`
- Vertex AI / GCP: `quota exceeded`, `resource exhausted`, `RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED`
- Generic: `daily quota`, `quota_exceeded`

The following phrases from the Ollama Cloud error should be added to the quota-exhaustion keyword list:

- `session usage limit`
- `upgrade for higher limits`

### Relevant config

```yaml
model:
  default: glm-5.2:cloud
  provider: ollama-jetson
fallback_providers: '[{"provider":"ollama","model":"gemma4:31b-mlx"},{"provider":"ollama-jetson","model":"gpt-oss:120b-cloud"},{"provider":"ollama","model":"nemotron3:33b"}]'
```

### Related issues

- #51677 — `feat(core): retry primary on transient 429 before falling back` — This PR added the transient-vs-quota 429 classification logic that checks for keywords like `quota`, `month`, `billing`, `insufficient_quota`. The Ollama Cloud error string doesn't match any of those keywords, which is the root cause of this bug.
- #60846 — `bug(gateway): provider 429 rate-limit surfaces as "Provider authentication failed"` — Related but different (429 misclassified as auth failure, not as transient rate limit).
- #59002 — `[Feature]: Bounded main-agent fallback when the active model hits quota or session limits` — Broader feature request; this bug is the specific blocker for that use case.

### Suggested fix

Add `"session usage limit"` and `"upgrade for higher limits"` to the quota-exhaustion keyword detection list (likely in `agent/agent_runtime_helpers.py` or `agent/conversation_loop.py` where the 429 error body is parsed for quota keywords).

items.title: [Bug]: Terminal/file tools fail with "Permission denied: '/root'" for all cron jobs after mixing root-launched and hermes-user-launched CLI sessions

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

items.body:
## Environment
- Deployment: systemd service (not Docker), Ubuntu 24.04, Hostinger VPS
- hermes-gateway runs as `User=hermes` (non-root, systemd unit sets `HOME=/home/hermes`, `HERMES_HOME=/home/hermes/.hermes` explicitly)
- Admin/CLI access is via a root-owned wrapper script (`/usr/local/bin/hermes`) that execs the venv binary directly
- Version at time of bug: v0.18.2 (2026.7.7.2), install method: git
- Confirmed still present after `hermes update` (pulled 1 new commit) and after a full `systemctl restart hermes-gateway`

## What happened
Around 2026-07-16 10:00 UTC, all cron jobs that use `terminal`, `read_file`, `write_file`, or `search_files` tools started failing with:

PermissionError: [Errno 13] Permission denied: '/root'

Full pattern from agent.log:
WARNING tools.environments.base: init_session failed (session=...): [Errno 13] Permission denied: '/root'; non-login probe: [Errno 13] Permission denied: '/root' — falling back to bash -l per command
WARNING tools.terminal_tool: Execution error, retrying in 2s (attempt 1/3) - Command: date +%F - Error: PermissionError: [Errno 13] Permission denied: '/root'
... (retries 3x with backoff, then fails)
WARNING agent.tool_executor: Tool write_file returned error (0.00s): {"error": "[Errno 13] Permission denied: '/root'"}
WARNING agent.tool_executor: Tool read_file returned error: {"error": "[Errno 13] Permission denied: '/root'"}
WARNING agent.tool_executor: Tool search_files returned error: {"error": "[Errno 13] Permission denied: '/root'"}

The cron job's LLM turn still completes "successfully" (agent sends a text-only Telegram reply), but every file-write step silently fails, so no actual output files are produced. This makes the failure easy to miss — `hermes cron list` shows `Last run: ok`.

## Suspected trigger
Before the bug appeared, I ran several `hermes cron create/edit/list` commands as plain root over SSH (instead of `sudo -u hermes hermes ...`) to manage jobs. I later found this left at least two root-owned files behind:

/home/hermes/.hermes/hermes-agent/hermes_cli/__pycache__/banner.cpython-311.pyc  (owner root:root)
/home/hermes/.hermes/hermes-agent/hermes_cli/__pycache__/build_info.cpython-311.pyc  (owner root:root)

matching a general pattern already reported in #16480 ("any file under $HERMES_HOME created by a root-launched CLI session can become inaccessible to the normal non-root runtime").

However, chown-ing these back to hermes:hermes and restarting hermes-gateway did NOT resolve the issue — the exact same Permission denied: '/root' errors persisted in the next cron run, so either there's another root-owned artifact I didn't find, or the actual cause is unrelated to file ownership (e.g. something in the terminal session's login-bash bootstrap in tools/environments/base.py around the init_session/_run_bash(..., login=True) call resolving HOME incorrectly for a reason independent of file ownership).

## Steps to reproduce (best guess)
1. Run `hermes cron create/edit/list ...` as root (not `sudo -u hermes hermes ...`) at least once while hermes-gateway runs as a non-root systemd user
2. Trigger any cron job that uses terminal/file tools (`hermes cron run <id>` or wait for schedule)
3. Observe `Permission denied: '/root'` in ~/.hermes/logs/agent.log for that job's session

## What I've tried (none fixed it)
- systemctl restart hermes-gateway
- hermes update --backup --yes (pulled 1 new commit, dependencies reinstalled, gateway restarted cleanly)
- chown-ing the two root-owned __pycache__/*.pyc files back to hermes:hermes, then restarting again

## Impact
Every cron job that writes files or runs shell commands silently produces no output while reporting success, which could easily go unnoticed for a while.
